Blazing Swan 2027: Side Quest
(24th – 30th March 2027, Jilakin Rock City, Kulin)

Life rarely follows the path imagined. We discover new avenues, change direction and sometimes get a little lost along the way. 

But so often, when we arrive, we find the people, places and pieces of ourselves quietly waiting for us to arrive. Thirteen detours and somehow you land exactly where you needed to be.

Sometimes, the best parts of a journey are the ones you never planned.

And then you realise its was never about the destination; it’s the journey itself. 

The deviations, the path less travelled… the side quests.

-----------

Blazing Swan 2027: “Side Quest” invites you to embrace the adventure, wander without a destination and find a familiar soul in an unfamiliar face. To deviate to find undiscovered art, or wander into the camp you hadn’t planned to visit. To immerse yourself in creativity, participate, play and perhaps... say “YES” a little more often.

Whilst on your Side Quest, we encourage you to live our 11 Principles. To embrace your curiosity, release your self-expression, share your gifts and to pick up some MOOP along the way as you get wonderfully lost amongst the community. Meet friends you don't know yet, welcome the stranger into your adventures, and stay up just long enough to welcome a sunrise. 

Nothing planned, but something wholesome, unplanned and magical experienced.

Between the dust, dancing, creating, gifting and the people we meet along the way, you might find yourself wondering…

Is Blaze the Side Quest? Or is everyday life simply the Side Quest that brings us home to the paddock, one more time?

Every path leads somewhere, but when the Side Quest becomes part of our story, the magic comes alive ... and it transforms into the ultimate adventure.

Blazing Swan 2027
 Side Quest 
 ~Take the Scenic Route

TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR

TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR is a new fair launched in 2025 by TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR (TABF), structured around networks within art book publishing. Through a format distinct from conventional fairs and its compact scale, it aims to activate the independent publishing scene in Japan and internationally, as well as exchanges among participants.

The shift from “TOKYO” to “TOKIO” signals an intentional repositioning: not as an alternative to TABF, but as a parallel platform offering a different perspective. This subtly “bootleg-like” naming reframes TABF’s alternative potential while embracing the heterogeneous, cross-cultural nature of art book publishing.

UPDATE - Thank you to everyone for their interest in this position, and thank you to those who applied. This position has now been filled. Please stay tuned to social media and the website for other volunteering opportunities.

----------------

Our Wellness Team looks after the event teams who build and packdown Blazing Swan, and we’re looking for someone to help lead the team and keep the whole thing running smoothly.

We’re looking for an organised, approachable human who’s good with people, can wrangle bookings and lead the volunteer team.

You’ll help coordinate the Wellness space, manage bookings and services, support and guide our volunteer crew and generally make sure things keep ticking along.

The role will focus on event setup and pack-down, with the first and last weeks of the event being the busiest. Hours will vary, with most Wellness services happening later in the day as you'll work around the crews' working hours.

You’ll have a 2IC and a team of Wellness volunteers to help make it happen.
Wellness experience is a bonus, but not essential. Being organised, friendly and good at making things happen is far more important.

Interested?

TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR(TABF) are pleased to announce that will participate in Under The Leaf - Book Fair, a two-day festival held in Helsinki, Finland.

During the fair, TABF will present 𝚄𝚗𝚍𝚎𝚛 𝚃𝚑𝚎 𝙻𝚒𝚗𝚎𝚜 an exhibition focusing on illustration and drawing. The exhibition will feature around 30 titles of art book and zines by artists based in Japan, published in recent years.

On the second day of the fair, Saturday, June 6, TABF founding member and project manager Naoko Higashi @naoko_higashi , together with Akira Kuroki @qrqi , director of TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR @tokioartbookfair , which launched last year, will give a talk introducing the activities of the fairs and the exhibition.

Hikari Nishida @hikanishida , artist and co-organizer of Under The Leaf – Book Fair, previously served as a curator for the Nordic Art Book Store as part of TABF 2023’s special program Guest Country vol.7: Nordic Countries. She also participated as a host exhibitor in last year’s TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR.

We are really looking forward to meeting everyone there.

—————————————

TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR(TABF)は、フィンランド・ヘルシンキで開催される「Under  The Leaf - Book Fair」に参加いたします。

TABFは期間中、イラストレーションとドローイングに焦点を当てた展示「Under The Lines」を会場内にて開催します。本展では、近年出版された日本を拠点とするTABFにゆかりのあるアーティストのアートブック、Zineなど約30タイトルを展示します。

Weather Preparation ☔☀️💨

Blazers! 4 days to go!! So let’s talk weather prep!

Cyclone Narelle will likely have finished dumping her fury before you arrive (remember to thank the crews currently slogging through it🙏), and we’re looking at mid-high 20’s in the daytime and down to about 10 degrees at night. 

THIS MEANS NOTHING AND WILL CHANGE, as Blaze can gift us 35 and sunny to 80km winds and storms to nearing zero at night, all in 1 day. It’s going to be the best, but we should all prepare for the worst 🤣⛺🪢

Tents, Gazebos & Wind
Whatever weather we get next week absolutely will involve wind. A lot! From all directions! Gazebos and tents often want to fly at Blaze. If you would like a tent to come back to, you absolutely need to tie/peg it down properly. 
Do this when you put your tent up, not at 4am when it’s already lifting off ✈
Use HEFTY stakes. If your pegs came free with your Kmart tent, they will not function. Buy better pegs!

Gazebos
Peg all the peg holes, tie guy ropes to all the eyelets; double pegging and two guy ropes per eyelet is better!Consider taking down gazebos overnight, when you're not there or when the winds pick up. Or use the best trick: tie your gear to your car/trailer, or other heavy objects like multiple large water containers. It can get rough out there, but usually cars do not want to fly 🙂❤️

Sun
Do what your mum says: slip, slop, slap, and get all the water inside you. Sun burn, dehydration and heat stroke are NOT fun!
Anti-sun
It can also get super cold at night out there: bring warm clothes, socks, blankets etc.

Rain
Bring extras in case of wet: warm socks, a rain jacket, gum boots, a positive outlook towards the rain our farmer friends would love 🌧️🌈
Add trenches around your tent, as the dry ground at Kulin can flood very quickly if it does rain. That means bring a shovel! 
Keep any electrics off the ground and not in what may become water 
Think about keeping any valuables or clothing off the floor of your tent, just in case it does rain or flood. Waterproof dry bags are also fab for important items like car keys, passports etc. 

Have fun packing, we can’t wait to see your shiny happy faces out there!! ❤️💕😊

What can a school of fish, a dolphin, an orca and a great white teach us about making change?⁠
 ⁠
Quite a lot, as it turns out.⁠
 ⁠
At the @surfersforclimate Water Women campout (@water.women.collective), we explored Bill Moyer's Four Roles of Social Change through an ocean lens, looking at the different ways people contribute to collective change.⁠
 ⁠
The key idea? There’s no hierarchy between the roles. Movements need different kinds of changemakers, and we can move between roles depending on what a moment calls for.⁠
 ⁠
Try mapping the roles across your own team, campaign or movement! ⁠
 ⁠
Thanks to Surfers for Climate for having us, and to everyone at Water Women who brought their experience, curiosity and care to the conversation.⁠
 ⁠
Workshop led by WELA's Cherry Muddle alongside Jess Bell, with session design supported by Kara Virik.⁠
⁠
Which role resonates most with you? Drop an emoji in the comments! 🐟🐬🐋🦈

⚞BYOD - BRING YOUR old DEVICE⚟

Wednesday 15 July at The Unconformity Hall 

Join us for The Unconformity's July's Open Hall, this month we're joined by Nancy Mauro-Flude, artist, educator and creative technologist, who will share insights into her practice and current work:

"Gather your gadgetry, blow off the dust, and join us in a collective hands-on tinkering and hacking session.

And as we gather to learn how old cats learn new tricks in screwdriver magnetism, we consider our daily agency-convenience ratios. 

Also as we tinker, we can touch on discussions around ideas of 'dependencies', these hands-on scrying acts of divining (not mining), suggest excentric approaches to holistic computing, think: spoon bending (not spoon feeding).

While gazing at the entrails of circuitry, embedded minerals and rainbow cabled wires, we can tell tales enchanting (and not uninspiring) Google Detox experiments, or the passionate tango of Facebook deplatforming dances. 

As we share stories of learning about computers, the hard way, we touch their inner parts with the soft, soft finger tips of our digits. 

We may even find ourselves imagining how an obsolete smartphone was left to rot, where the slime mould creeps, in the dark murky brew it transformed into something other...

+ We strive to include interested participants of all backgrounds, knowledge and experience levels. Curious people are especially welcome. 

+ More of a collective hacking and experimentation session than a rote learning instruction format, guided by the premise: "The symbols of the divine initially show up at the trash stratum. — Philip K. Dick 🝐 ⚶ ♆"

Attendees are invited to bring an old electronic device that you are happy to tinker with. We recommend devices that can be carried in your hands, please no smoke alarms or leaking batteries.

During the Open Hall we will also be sharing updates on Secret Station, launching the program and West Coast Presale tickets for our October 3 event with the West Coast Wilderness Railway.

The ocean should be safe for every woman, but it hasn’t been.

To every woman who’s spoken up recently, we believe you. Saying it out loud takes courage, and every story makes it easier for the next woman to tell hers.

It isn’t that every guy is an abuser, it’s that most men enable a toxic culture by staying quiet. From where she stands, there’s no difference between the guy who laughs at a sexual joke and the one who looks away. And yet, nearly all of those men would still say they’re one of the good ones.

Surf culture has used women’s bodies to sell products for too long. Ads that show female pro surfers from the neck down. Magazine covers with a man in a barrel and a woman on the sand. Comment sections that talk about a woman’s body more than her surfing.

Change has to happen everywhere. Brands deciding who goes on the billboard and what she’s doing. Contests and sponsors with proper safeguarding and real consequences. 

Boardriders clubs with codes of conduct that actually get enforced. And guys calling each other out in the line up as soon as they hear toxic behaviour.

We stand with every woman who has spoken up, and every woman who isn’t ready to yet. You never have to carry it by yourself. We created Water Women for you.

If you need support, call 1800RESPECT on 1800 737 732, text 0458 737 732 or visit 1800respect.org.au. In an emergency, call 000.

⛽️ ⛽️ FUEL UPDATE ⛽️ ⛽️
️
Blazing Swan has been closely monitoring increasing fuel costs and fuel scarcity in regional towns and working with our contractors and our friends in Kulin to make plans for the Blazing Swan event.

Currently, the Kulin self-service petrol station is open from 8am to 5pm daily with ULP.

However, the diesel supply in Kulin and surrounding towns such as Corrigin still faces uncertainty.

Most regional petrol stations still have restrictions in place.

Attendees should still be able to plan their journey to get to and from Blazing Swan 2026.

 We recommend:

Consider stopping at multiple service stations along the way to refuel. This will help spread the load in the area and if one service station does not have fuel you will not be caught short
Consider carpooling where possible – check out our rideshare Facebook group to meet others travelling to the event.

ULP/ petrol drivers - Blazing Swan requests those travelling with unleaded fuel do not bring jerry cans to the event.

Diesel drivers – If you need to bring additional fuel with you we request you top up your tank to empty your jerry cans prior to entering Blazing Swan. Please do so in the marked space at the 24 Hours Fuel Kulin Station. This will reduce the amount of fuel on site and the potential for spillages.

If you are planning to bring diesel with you to Blazing Swan please refer to the website for further information on the storing and transporting fuel safely. Information will be provided shortly.

Vehicles will be checked for fuel and turned away if this process is not followed.

Again, if you are concerned about attending Blazing Swan we are offering a full refund or deferred ticket to next year’s event.

We thank you for your assistance in helping creating a safe environment for us to build our Blazing Swan village.

Blazing Swan Committee

Website Info: http://www.blazingswan.com.au
Refunds: https://events.humanitix.com/blazing-swan-2026-takes-a-village

📍🏰 Centre Kiosk — Your Central Hub at Blazing Swan

Located at the castle in the centre of the village. Welcome, Burners 

What you’ll find at Centre Kiosk:
❓ Information, Concierge & Service Desk
Got questions? Need directions? Not sure what’s happening or where to go? Our team is here to help with the what, where, how, why… and maybe.

🗺️ Sitemap & Navigation
A large central map will be available so you can easily find Theme Camps, art installations, key locations, and activities across the event.

🧊 Ice Sales — The Ice Vault
Ordered ice? We’ve got you covered. Centre Kiosk is home to the Ice Vault, run by our legendary Ice Maidens & Ice Men. Ice will be available at separately scheduled times for Theme Camps and for General Campers, with collection times clearly displayed at the counter.

💼 Lost Property
Found something? Bring it to Centre Kiosk. Lost something? Come check in with us — we’ll do our best to reunite you with your lost treasures as soon as possible, and after the event if not.

Theme Camps can bring lost items to Centre Kiosk to be stored safely, and we will also try to reunite these with their owners. You’re encouraged not to leave all lost property until the final day — staggered drop-offs help us return items faster and handle the volume 

Come say hi, get your bearings, grab your ice, and let us help you make the most of your burn 🦢 ❤️

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 The Institute of Critical Zoologists (ICZ) 💬
Singapore Art Book Fairは、この地域におけるインディペンデント出版や実験的なブックプラクティスを育んできた存在として、以前から敬意を持って見てきました。アーティストやデザイナー、小規模な出版社が出会い、アイデアを交換し、新たな観客とつながる場を生み出しています。多様な声や型にはまらない形式を大切にしている点も印象的で、現代のアート出版に関心を持つ人々にとって重要な場となっています。

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Thumb Books 💬
レネー・ティン（Renée Ting）が運営するプラットフォーム Thing Booksは、シンガポールのアートブックシーンの成長において非常に大きな影響力を持ってきました。長年続くSingapore Art Book Fair（SGABF）の主催者であり、アートブックを表現の媒体として発展させ、広めるためのさまざまな取り組みを行ってきた存在として、コミュニティの多くがThing Booksとレネーに敬意を抱き、インディペンデント出版のシーンを支え続けるその姿勢に励まされています。Thumb Booksは、まさにThing Booksが育ててきた土壌から芽吹いた存在とも言えます。本を出版する人にとって、それを流通させ、世界に届けるための場がなければ成立しません。私自身も、レネーが働いていた書店で販売するためにジンを制作し始め、2016年には他の若いブックメーカーたちとブースを共有して初めてSGABFに参加しました。そして2017年には、地元のアートスペースの一員として本を販売していた際にSGABFでRenéeと出会いました。それから時を経て、現在では私たちは結婚し、同じホームスタジオを拠点にThing BooksとThumb Booksをそれぞれ運営しています。

-

◎ 𝘎𝘶𝘦𝘴𝘵
｜The Institute of Critical Zoologists (ICZ)
(Singapore, Singapore)
@robert_zhao 

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Thing Books 💬
アーティスト ロバート・ジャオ・レンフイ（Robert Zhao Renhui）は、「The Institute of Critical Zoologists」の名のもとで書籍を出版しており、その作品は動物を人間がどのように見るかという「動物学的まなざし」に対して批評的にアプローチしています。彼は2013年のSingapore Art Book Fairの第1回に出展し、それ以来継続してアーティストブックを制作してきました。シンガポールにおいてアーティストブックというジャンルをいち早く推進した存在のひとりであり、多くの若いアーティストに自身の本やジンを制作するきっかけを与えています。

(Singapore, Singapore)

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Thing Books 💬
Thumb Booksは、シンガポールのアーティスト ライ・ユートン（Lai Yu Tong）によって設立された小さな出版社で、子どもと大人の両方に向けた本を制作しています。ユートンは、ドローイングやイメージ制作、彫刻、音などを横断しながら活動しています。人がイメージを生み出し、物語を語ることへの根源的な欲求を前提に、現在を表現するためのメディアを探り続けています。私たちは、彼が美術学生としてジンを作り始めた頃からその活動を見てきました。この12年のあいだに、彼のアートブック制作が深い感受性とともに発展していく様子を感じています。

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Ke Xu 💬
謎めいた「EBOOKS」に出会う前に、まず彼らの本に出会いました。そこには、通じ合うようなユーモアと、言葉にされない精度が満ちています。SGABFで『Typeface』を見つけて持ち帰ることができたことは、とても幸運でした。その後、『英語が分からないので、この本を使って会話させてください。』というプロジェクトを知りました。機知に富んだセルフパブリッシングのガイドであり、リラックスして読むことで初めて気づくようなささやかな知恵を、親しみやすいかたちで伝えてくれます。直近のTABFでは、見知らぬ来場者が私のブースを訪れ、私の作品にあるコンセプトやユーモアに気づいてくれました。まるで本を通じて再会した旧友のように、私たちはすぐに打ち解けました。

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Tomomi Mizukoshi 💬
EBOOKSの素朴でくだらないアイデアがとても好きです。かわいくてホッとするのもから奇妙なものまで様々ですが、中身のゆるさに対して造本が決まっているところも魅力です。2023年のTABFで隣のブースになったことで知り合いましたが、横でずっと解説を聞いていたので私もEBOOKSの本を接客できるまでになり贅沢な体験でした。今回も楽しみです。

-

@xu_ke_

アートブックを制作していると、時々思いがけない嬉しい出会いに恵まれます。Keさんと仲良くなれたのも、昨年末のアートブックフェアがきっかけでした。Keさんのアートブックは、小さなアート作品のようで、1冊ごとに異なるコンセプトをスマートに表現されています。また、自費出版で制作を続けている点にも惹かれました。TOKIO ART BOOK FAIRで多くの人に紹介できることを楽しみにしています。

水越さんとは以前TABFで席が隣になったことをきっかけに知り合い、その後も不思議な交流が続いています。水越さんのイラストは、独特な表現の中にもなぜか共感できるポイントが散りばめられていて、何度見ても飽きません。イラストとアートブックとの相性もぴったりで、様々な手法で刷られたアートブックの中には、独自のカラフルでユニークな世界が広がっています。今回またご一緒に出展できることをとても嬉しく思っています。

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Loose Joints Publishing 💬
フォルカ・レナー（Volker Renner）はLoose Jointsと継続的に協働している作家であり、大胆で遊び心のあるセルフパブリッシングを体現する、意欲的で実験的なブックメーカーです。

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Pfeil Magazine 💬
フォルカと私は、時期は異なりますが、ハンブルクの同じ美術大学で学びました。フォルカーの本はどれも独自の作品であり、本棚に加えるべき一冊としてすべておすすめです。

◎ 𝘎𝘶𝘦𝘴𝘵
｜Loose Joints Publishing
(London, United Kingdom / Marseille, France)
@jointsloose 

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 volker renner 💬
Loose Jointsは、ルイス・チャップリン（Lewis Chaplin）とサラ・ピエゲ・エスプノン（Sarah Piegay Espenon）によって2014年に共同設立されたインディペンデントな写真出版レーベルです。現代の写真集やアーティストによる出版物を手がけ、フォトグラファーやヴィジュアルアーティストと密接に協働しています。編集、デザイン、制作をインハウスで行い、コンセプトに基づいた丁寧な造本で知られています。編集方針としては、新進や十分に紹介されてこなかった写真家の声や、フォトブックという形式における実験的な語りの方法に焦点を当てています。ロンドンで小さなサイドプロジェクトとして始まり、現在はマルセイユを拠点とする信頼あるインディペンデント出版社へと成長し、写真集専門の書店兼ギャラリー「Ensemble」も運営しています。アーティストとの緊密な協働と、写真を用いた先進的で物語性のある表現を重視する出版活動によって、高い評価を得ています。

-

◎ 𝘎𝘶𝘦𝘴𝘵
｜Pfeil Magazine
(Hamburg, Germany)
@pfeilmagazine 

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 volker renner 💬
Pfeil Magazineは、アンヤ・ディートマン（Anja Dietmann）が編集し、ロンドンを拠点とする出版社Montez Pressから2012年より刊行されているインディペンデントなアート／カルチャー雑誌です。「雑誌という形式による展覧会」として構想されています。各号はひとつの言葉やテーマ（たとえば「Love」「Bread」「Friend」「High」「Body」など）を軸に構成され、アーティストや作家がその言葉に応答するかたちでテキストやイメージ、実験的な寄稿を行い、美術、理論、文学が交差する複数著者による出版物となっています。レイアウトは各ページを想像上の展示空間における「床・壁・天井」として扱う構成となっており、雑誌全体がキュレーションされた印刷による展覧会として機能します。実験的な編集形式と分野横断的な寄稿によって、アーティスト出版、展覧会カタログ、コンセプチュアルアートプロジェクトのあいだに位置づけられる雑誌です。

｜Bong Sadhu

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Cosmic jam 💬
同世代でありながら、お店を運営をしつつ展示の開催や海外のブックフェアにも積極的に参加する二人の活動には、大きな刺激を感じています。インディペンデントを軸に、ハンドメイドで一つ一つに魂を込めた作品などを生み出し、自分たちの手の届く範囲で純粋な表現を追求している姿勢が印象的です。また、同世代で似た方向を向く仲間たちを巻き込みながら、場やムーブメントを生み出している点にも強く惹かれます。彼らの生活や遊びから自然に派生する作品には、常に彼ら自身の視点がしっかりと息づいている気がします。

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 dig around round 💬
江の島にあるAce General Storeを通じてBong Sadhuと出会いました。Ace General Storeは、私が「Guruguru Brain clouds & waves 7-inch series」で協働した友人たちが運営するショップです。このシリーズは四季に沿って展開されたアナログ盤のみのヴァイナル・プロジェクトで、各レコードのスリーブは季節を反映するよう手染めされています。Bong Sadhuは、台湾でのある長い春のあいだに私の最初の本『（ww） ROOTS』を取り扱ってくれ、それ以来、私たちは友人です。彼らの活動は、美術、印刷、インディペンデント出版を、独特の好奇心と丁寧さとともに結びつけています。

-

(Tokyo, Japan)
@cosmicjam_ 

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Bong Sadhu 💬
Cosmic Jamは僕らBong Sadhuの一つ下の年齢の作家ユニットで、幹人と優人は同じスタジオの後輩でもあり、喜多は僕らの店でも昨年展示をしてくれました。活動形態がすごく似ていて、年齢的にも少し後輩なポジションでもあるのかな？今回、ぜひ出展してよと両者一致で声かけさせていただきました。僕らが彼らの製作物について説明するよりも、独自の世界観のある作品を是非直接見て素直に感じてほしいと思います。

アオちゃんは僕らのホームエリアである片瀬江ノ島の「Ace General Store」を通して出会い、パートナーのGoくんがGuruguru BrainというレーベルオーナーでMaya Ongakuがレコードのリリースもしています。そういったホームでの活動のつながりで出会い、お店の開店のときに彼女のリサーチブック「Roots」を書店に置かせてもらいました。今回は福岡から来てくれて、新作本に加えてコラボグッズなどもリリース予定です。一緒のブースに出れることをとても嬉しく思います。

The Goodwillerのプロジェクトを知り、すぐにファンになりました。 Zineの制作に関わるすべてを独自のセンスで手がけ、前例のないプロジェクトを展開する彼女たちはとても魅力的で、リスペクトしています。 「洋服の循環」を表現し、同じ志を持つ仲間だと感じています！

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 Robineggpie 💬
2024年の「Unlimited Edition」の交流を通して、私はTOKYO ART BOOK FAIRに参加し、アーティストトークの中でThe Goodwillerを知りました。彼らのジン制作のプロセス（地元の古着を仕入れ、修復し、スタイリングし、再販売する）は、実践的なアートの優れた例です。サステナビリティと公共との関わりを両立させる理想的な方法を見出しています。

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 藤田紗衣 💬
The Goodwillerの田岡さんとは雪の降る新潟で、斉藤さんとはあるホームパーティの暗がりの中で初めて出会いました。デザイナーとアーティストの2人が行うこのプロジェクトは、セカンドハンドストアを利用した新たな循環のアイディアをユニークに軽やかに提案してくれます。

𝘍𝘳𝘰𝘮 室井悠輔 💬
私はモノを集めることが好きだが、手放すのが苦手だ。増えすぎて箱の奥に押し込むこともある。The Goodwillerの活動を眺めていると、つくることで生活をポジティブに変換するヒントを教えてくれる。

Let’s Talk Decommodification! ❌💲

We all know Blazing Swan is a commercialism-free space, but decommodifying your burn can include so much more.

Today’s example: do you need a new fab outfit haul from bleeping Temu? Of course you don’t!  Consider supporting local artists, crafting, gifting or upcycling instead; vintage treasures from Marketplace or buy nothing groups can make your look unique without feeding the fast fashion industrial complex. Plus they likely won’t disintegrate on Day 2

Benefits of decommodification:
🗑Stop filling the planet up with single-use trash
💸Save  for that Blaze ticket and your rent
🌟Stop feeding the stupid algo and stand out from the crowd
👨‍🎨Getting crafty with friends and modifying what you’ve already got is the way to go
😏Or just be naked, naked is 🤗

Help us all resist the substitution of consumption for participatory experience!

KIRTIは、東南アジア各地の新興現代美術シーンを探るアート・アーカイブおよびインタビュー・イニシアティブです。地域の出版環境の制約に応じて立ち上げられた「KIRTI」は、ローカルなアートスペースを通じて研究を非制度的に循環させるDIY出版物を制作しています。

2012年にnos:booksから初めての本の制作に誘われたことが、私たちの最初の出会いでした。この協働を通して、アート出版の広がりある可能性に気づき、絵画やドローイングの発表の仕方が大きく変わりました。卓越した制作力に加え、nos:booksは独自のユーモアをもって「本」という概念に常に問いを投げかけています。

Hello Blazers 🔥🔥

📍Our general camping will look a little bit different at Blaze this year!
There are a few reasons for this, including:
1. Safety – Best practice for safe camping at large events is always evolving, and we have agreed to trial a new layout.
2. Space – with a record number of people coming to Blaze this year we need to ensure that there is space for everyone.

As you can see from the map, there are different camping areas:
⛺Tents only camping – this is an area for ground tents and swags. You will park your car in the ‘parking’ area after dropping off your equipment.
⛺🚐Mixed camping – for tents and cars and other vehicles
👨‍👩‍👧Family camping – cars, tents and other vehicles will still need to make their best efforts to separate
🚐Vehicles only - for caravans, vans, rooftop tents etc, no ground tents in this area
🅿Parking - No camping or sleeping in vehicles in this area. We have arranged extra security around this area.

Please note that this map is subject to change at the event, depending on things like volume in different camping areas.

✨Camping in a mixed group?
If you're planning to camp with friends and you have a mixed group of tents, campers and rooftop tents you should aim to camp in the mixed camping areas.

We will not actively prevent people from camping together; however, you may not be able to have space around you for your friends to come later. If you would like to camp with your friends, we encourage you to arrive at the event together. This has always been the case at Blaze.

We do have Accessibility Camping (ACC) available, to discuss please contact accessibility@blazingswan.com.au

The camping format for 2026 will be a trial and we WELCOME you to submit feedback to us AFTER the event.

Also please note, that any aggression or un-Blazey behaviour, especially towards our Traffic volunteers will not be tolerated in anyway. We are all working together to build our cohesive village.

Any questions can be directed to traffic@blazingswan.com.au
Thanks for your understanding - we cannot wait to see you in the dust!!!🔥🥰💖

東京の書店で初めてSAMY PRESSの本に出会いました。それ以来、その本を集め、他の人にも紹介したいと思うようになりました。SAMY PRESSがアーティストブックに向き合う姿勢には、コンセプトと物質性の両面において強く惹かれています。彼らの出版物は、繊細で独自の視点から立ち上がることが多いです。それらをめくることで、日常のささやかな観察に対する感受性が呼び起こされます。この繊細さは現在の瞬間にとどまるものではなく、時間とともにゆっくりと展開していきます。

「出版」という行為自体を捉え直そうとする姿勢に共感します。近年の独立系出版やアーティスツ・ブック、リトルプレスの隆盛の中で、歴史的な文脈を踏まえ、日本では未訳の重要文献を紹介する出版芸術工房（Publishing Arts Workshop）の活動は、今日の出版にまつわるあらゆる実践者にとって重要な視座を与えてくれるものだと思います。

The Unconformity is seeking applications for their next Chair, Board of Directors.

Applications are sought from executive leaders with strategic arts, cultural, tourism or regional interest or experience, for a three-year term.

The preferred candidate would be a respected leader with senior experience, strong external relationships across government and philanthropy, and the ability to connect artistic ambition with organisational sustainability.

Applicants would have a connection with or interest in the arts, or remote and regional communities, with a preference to the West Coast of Lutruwita/Tasmania.

We believe diversity strengthens our team, and we welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. If you believe you are a strong candidate, we encourage your application, even if you don’t meet all the criteria. 

Enquiries are to be emailed to The Unconformity Deputy Chair, Chloe Tanner deputychair@theunconformity.com.au

To find out more, including the full Position Description and Strategic Plan, visit theunconformity.com.au/work-with-us/.

To apply, please submit your application via the form on our website, together with your CV, by 11:59pm AEDT on Wednesday 23 September 2026. 

A selection panel will assess applications and make recommendations to the Board for consideration. All enquiries and applications will be treated confidentially.

EFFIGY ACTIVITIES & ENTERTAINMENT

At the heart of our annual gathering stands our Effigy

 This is not a structure to pass by, but a place to enter. A place to gather our intentions, as this event has been shaped by the hands, ideas, and generosity of its people, and within this space is an invitation to continue that tradition!
This is a centre built not just to be seen, but to be used!

We invite you to please sign up to our Effigy Scheduling Platform to create, connect, and host your own moments within it — whether that’s a small workshop, a conversation circle, a shared meal, a performance, or a Bar Takeover!

Set on land where First Nation Communities once met to share knowledge, trade, and make collective decisions, this space exists to bring people together again in that same spirit.

If you feel the pull to gather others, listen to it. If you carry something to share, this is the place! So come add your voice, your presence, and your spark.
Step into the village centre and shape the moment!

TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR 2026 will take place over three days, from Friday 1 May to Sunday 3 May 2026, at Shiba Park Hotel.

TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR 2026 is a fair organised by TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR and built around networks in art book publishing. The second edition will take place over three days, from Friday 1 May to Sunday 3 May 2026, at Shiba Park Hotel. A total of 52 exhibitors, including artists, publishers, bookshops, and galleries from Japan and abroad, will gather, each developing their own activities through publications such as art books and zines.

The fair uses an invitation-based format, in which participating exhibitors invite other exhibitors to join. Making use of the setting of Shiba Park Hotel, known as a “Library Hotel,” the fair hopes to encourage exchanges among participants and bring more energy to the independent publishing scene in Japan and abroad.

We very much look forward to welcoming you.

Looking back at this festival season with some distance I believe this show in Portugal was my favorite. So much love and attention from the audience-almost too good to be true. 

What’s funny is that most musicians on big stages play with so called in ear monitors nowadays. Which means you don’t actually hear the crowd that well. When I then saw the second clip that was filmed from stage I got goosebumps when I heard how many people were singing along.

It’s still crazy to me that people all over the world seem to know my songs. A heart felt thank you to everyone who came out this year. Hopefully see you soon!

Much love, PJ

The Unconformity is excited to announce our three Ongoing Artists.

Welcome to our three Ongoing Artists: Stevie Battese, Iris Blazely, and Nancy Mauro-Flude.

Over the next 18 months, the artists will spend time embedded within The Unconformity, developing new ideas and creative works shaped through a long-term, supported engagement with people, place, and environment.

Bringing together a diverse range of artistic practices, perspectives, and approaches, each artist will contribute something distinct and unique to The Unconformity and the West Coast community. Their projects promise to open new conversations, connections, and ways of experiencing Queenstown and its surrounds, breaking boundaries across both traditional and experimental mediums.

The Ongoing Artist program creates space for experimentation, collaboration, and deep creative inquiry. We’re looking forward to sharing more as their projects unfold.

We’re proud to be a part of the Experimental Commissioning Consortium (ECC) – a new multi-year, multi-organisation initiative that scaffolds independent artists to make ambitious work.

The ECC is a newly convened group of organisations around Australia devoted to the development and presentation of independent and experimental art and performance. It seeks to foster cross-sector collaboration to generate increased mobility and opportunity for artists. 

The program includes three pillars: an experimental laboratory to incubate work, a commissioning circle to bring work into development, and a national touring network. 

Participating organisations: Abbotsford Convent (@abbotsfordconvent), Arts House (@artshouse), Assembly 197 (@assembly.197), Cementa (@cementafestival), Dancehouse (@dancehouse.melb), Metro Arts (@metroarts), PACT (@pact_sydney), Performance Space, PICA (@pica_perth), Punctum (@punctuminc), Superposition (@superpositionfestival), The Substation (@thesubstation), The Unconformity (@theunconformity), Utp (@utp___), Vitalstatistix (@vitalstatistix_), Wired Lab (@thewiredlab). The ECC is supported by Creative Australia (@creative.australia).

In 2022, Luke George spent time on the West Coast, supported by The Unconformity's Artist In Residence program. Luke grew up in Tarraleah, the son of a hydro worker. Returning to his roots in Lutruwita/Tasmania and spending time at a local working sawmill inspired the development of Fell: a work that sees Luke suspended in the air with a log equal to his weight.

Fell first premiered at The Substation and visited Liveworks Festival before returning west – performed in Queenstown inside a working sawmill. The work commenced with audiences joining Luke in the wood yard to select his collaborating log and carry it inside, guided by fellow audience members.

We extend our heartfelt thanks to Pioneer Traders Tasmania for their support of the festival and for inviting contemporary performance into an active industrial space.

✨Blaze without Barriers - Accessibility Crew (ACC) ✨

You belong here. And you don’t have to push yourself to participate a certain way to be part of Blazing Swan.

ACC offers dedicated Accessibility Camping to help with reduced travel distances, flatter terrain, easier access to toilets (including accessible toilets/showers), key services, and access to power where required.

Participants can attend with registered assistance animals and support workers as part of their access needs. Please reach out to us ASAP if you have assistance animals coming as we need to make sure we have a few extra details recorded!

We’re here to help you plan for sustainability, whether that’s mobility access, sensory care, medication safety, quieter spaces, or simply pacing yourself. Support is available, and we encourage you to reach out before or during the event.

Participation can look like resting, observing, staying close to camp, or leaving early. All of it counts.

If you think Accessibility Camping or other supports may help you participate more safely and comfortably, please connect with us early at accessibility@blazingswan.com.au

In 2025, The Unconformity facilitated a Photography Mentorship Program alongside the festival, aiming to support professional pathways for arts and event photographers on the West Coast. The program enabled a team of West Coast–based photographers to gain professional-level experience, industry mentorship, and build their portfolios through real-world festival documentation.

Participants were paired with a professional documentation mentor to guide them throughout the festival. During the festival, photographers documented public art installations, live performances, visual art, and audience experiences, producing a collection of images that reflected the spirit of the festival while deepening their technical abilities and understanding of arts and event photography.

The program supported The Unconformity’s commitment to regional storytelling and helped create pathways for participants toward future professional work in arts, events, and tourism. Thanks to West Coast Wilderness Railway for supporting this initiative.

Still taking in what it meant to be part of the @savethewavescoalition Film Festival in Ericeira✨

Having our film screened at an event of this caliber, and seeing our short film travel around the world, means so much to me. Not only because of the incredible films and names we had the privilege of standing alongside, but especially because of everything Save The Waves stands for and the work they do to protect our oceans and coastlines.

Sitting there in Ericeira, I found myself thinking back to when I first started filming on the beach in Jacó, Costa Rica. Just a camera, the ocean, and a passion for telling stories.

Many thanks to @save_azores_waves for giving us the opportunity to share this video with the world.

A big thank you to @miguelbaratadealmeida and the whole team for putting together such a special event, and for the opportunity to present our film and share the stage with @_miguelblanco_ 

It was also so good to see some unexpected familiar faces, to watch our film on a screen in a place like this, and to see how passion projects and genuine stories can bring people together.

And above all, thank you @peterhealion. For opening the doors of your home to me, for sharing your story, and for believing in this idea from the very beginning.

Grateful for every part of the journey 🌊

Jessee Lee Johns first visited Queenstown from his home state of Western Australia in December 2024 to undertake a residency with The Unconformity. He returned in 2025 to present The Commonwealth of New Bayswater at The Unconformity 2025 festival.

Across the festival weekend, Queenstown was the temporary home of The Commonwealth of New Bayswater: a constantly mutating micro-nation, populated by visa-holding festival audiences and citizen artist Jessee Lee Johns.

Jessee spent three months on the West Coast in the lead up to the festival – foraging for found objects and building the latest iteration of New Bayswater from scratch. With the option of either a working or tourist visa, guests could earn New Bayswater Dollars at the content mine, produce cultural exports for the gallery, buy and sell wares at the convenience store, or simply pull up a seat at the workers club.

💌Introducing the Blazing Swan Telegram Channel!

Following on from online discussions about how we can try to be more effective with our event/org communications, we've launched a Telegram channel.

As you'll be aware, using Meta is getting harder and harder to communicate to the community, so we're going to try some new methods and some diversification. And this includes this change. 

The aim of introducing Telegram is not to replace or split The Blazing Swan Community Page or any other group or page we have, everything will continue as normal. Instead, this change is about providing an additional and an alternative way for the community to get information.

The channel will only post official event/org information - it will mirror all information and announcements provided online - so you don't have to change if you're happy with how things are. But because there are no text discussion/response feedback options (other than emojis) and no way for users to post - it will help provide a decluttered 'outgoing/broadcast' channel of communications direct from Blazing Swan.

Think of it like emails - but without spam filters.

We hope this change provides the community with a clearer and more organised way to access official communications.

For those in the community who want to be in the know, but not overloaded with the comments etc of the group - this is an alternative way to do that.

We've run internal tests before launching, and it's been live with the membership for the last couple of weeks... and now launching to the wider community.

We recommend reading our more in depth thoughts about this change here that may answer any questions or concerns you have:
https://blazingswan.com.au/announcing-telegram-for-blazing-swan/

Once you have downloaded the app, you can join the channel here:
https://t.me/+BodVLueCUes4M2Y1

As ever, any thoughts and feedback - publicly can be discussed here, and privately can be sent to comms@blazingswan.com.au

Ultimately, we don't know if this will help to solve our thoughts and concerns - but stepping forward and trying something new is, just like our temporary community in the dust once a year, an experiment.

Napier is a town of resilience; in the 1930s when the ground lifted and shock for 2 mins at 7.8 on the Richter scale, everything they knew was lost, and over 1% of the population perished. Yet its people gathered from the rubble and actively made a decision to rebuild - to be modern, simple, and beautiful! 
.
The @art_deco_napier trust was established in the 1980s to ensure the story of that resilience is shared and the beauty of its heritage architecture preserved. Today I got to experience their mid-winter walking tour and I highly recommend it - plus Bev our guide was fabulously passionate! Check it out, if ever in Napier!

caption:
Este não foi o meu primeiro ano como criativa no Portuguese Surf Film Festival (já ando por aqui desde 2020), mas esta edição foi particularmente especial: 15 anos de Festival!

Comecei por pensar num conceito que ligasse os 15 anos à Ericeira e ao surf: uma linha, a linha que conta os anos de histórias. E a partir dessa linha fui construindo toda a identidade visual desta edição.

Azul, vermelho, ondas, cinema, Ericeira.
Uma identidade que acabou por sair do papel e ocupar a Casa da Cultura, o festival e toda a comunicação.

E claro… não coloquei aqui tudo, senão tínhamos um Reel de 10 minutos. 😂

Ficaram de fora a identidade da Ocean Art, todo o merchandising, todas as peças digitais, social media, materiais de comunicação… enfim, muita coisa.

Também não consegui filmar toda a equipa e todo o processo (desculpem lá, não dá para estar sempre com o telemóvel na mão).

Mas não podia deixar de falar da minha enorme admiração pela @susana.metzger e pela @fezandavalli , as principais responsáveis por tornar este magnífico evento possível. É um privilégio fazer parte disto.

Um enorme obrigada à @camara_municipal_mafra pelo apoio, à @imagemplana pelo profissionalismo na montagem de toda a decoração do espaço, em tão pouco tempo (vocês são os maiores) e a todos os parceiros e patrocinadores que fizeram parte desta edição.

E obrigada ao Surf Film por me deixar continuar a contar estas histórias, à minha maneira. 

See you next year!

There is something about people coming together.
Singing , dancing
or simply just being together sharing stories .
Something so  ancient 
that remembers us of times where
this was all there was .
Nowdays we gather  for few days and when we leave we go with our heart full
Because we allowed ourselves to be who we truly are
Behind masks that society taught us to wear
We go with a feeling of having returned home
And we leave with a feeling of home sick 

I wonder if this small portion of what we live there shouldn't be the normal?

There we can be vulnerable, there everything is so much intense because we live with an open heart without the fear of being hurt or maybe a little bit more brave because we feel we are in a safe container and if we do end up hurt we know we are being hold.

We dare to love, 
We dare to let go of what we thought we were 
We dare to explore who we truly are 
What our hearts really desire
What we came here for 

And the answers comes as a whisper 

Just be still
Open you heart 
Come back to yourself 
There is nothing to achieve
Nothing to become 
Nothing to prove
Get yourself out of the way 
Surrender to this moment 
As it is 
Is all there is 
Let your tears fall down
and let them become one with the rain
Get barefoot 
Dance freely 
Open your voice 
Take care of yourself 
Let go of your identity 
It's safe to die 
You will not die 
You will come to life 

Oh so much to still integrate 
So much ( love) to share 

And is not all rainbows and unicorns 
There is also deep pain 
But there is the choice to go deep down that trail knowing you will come back more like yourself
than ever 
You let go of everything
and everything comes back to you 

Devotion was my word for this year's festival 
I have felt a devotion through chanting and singing that I have never felt before 
I only wish to keep this in my heart and forever remember that everything I have ever wanted is already

HERE, NOW

I have only gratitude in my heart for all of you that we shared even just a smile
You are not all in these pictures 
But you are in my heart 

Forever ♾️ 

and this is not a promise 

This is the

TRUTH

We are always together 

Wellcome back home 🤗

Dale's Snapper vs Kirra fist raise ✊

Did you experience Flotsam's Focal Point in AR? One of the new additions to this year's Flotsam Festival was the use of augmented reality to bring surf images to life. 

By scanning the Focal Point outdoor photo installations, visitors unlocked stories, interviews and archival footage connected to the images on display - preserving not just iconic moments, faces and places, but the memories and voices behind them.

This installation paired an iconic image of Dale Richards from a momentous 2012 Kirra swell. Footage from @shaggamang of Dale at Snapper was superimposed over the photograph by @sweetocean to show Dale in motion - fists firmly raised in both captures

Once one of the region's finest up and comers, Dale rocked the surfing world when he won the Quiksilver Pro Trials in 2007 and in doing so, become one of the first aboriginal surfers to compete in a WCT event - paving the way for the current crop of standout indigenous talent putting their stamp on the lineup

Focal Point exhibition is Flotsam's interactive archive of Gold Coast surf culture, connecting generations through the stories that shape our coastline. Flotsam's Focal Point installations are packed away for another year, but the images live on.

Maybe evolution isn’t always about becoming something new.
Sometimes it’s about remembering how to be together.

To move together.
To breathe together.
To dance with people who were strangers yesterday and somehow don’t feel like strangers anymore.

That’s what stayed with me from this year’s Yoga del Mar Spirit Festival.

My second year here, reconnecting with beautiful people from last year, meeting new souls and artists, and experiencing again something quite rare: there is almost no line between artist and attendee.

We practice together, eat together, dance together, celebrate together. Everyone becomes part of the experience.

And maybe that is its own kind of evolution, when the individual becomes part of something collective, without losing who they are.

Very grateful for the music, the movement, the conversations, the familiar faces and the new ones.

But mostly, for the human connection behind all of it.

Thank you, Yoga del Mar family. 🤍
Until next time.

Our latest Moonland release is now live featuring eight written works developed from the inaugural Moonland Retreat.

In 2025, a group of people came together on the West Coast for four days. Some identified as artists, as writers, as researchers, or as poets, from places near and far. This was the first Moonland Retreat, an invitation to sense and share the environment of Queenstown and surrounds through written words.

Over the course of the retreat, writers grounded on country, roamed the roads, peered into archives, and exchanged ways of working. This publication shares the stories they found, a set of signals transmitted from the West Coast to the world.

Moonland itself is an ever-changing platform devoted to sharing the memories, stories, ideas, research and realities of this place. Read the latest release here: moonland.theunconformity.com.au

FUSO – International Video Art Festival of Lisbon – was part of the Biennial’s program, presenting a selection inspired by the theme Gestures of Abundance, curated by Claire Shea, Fatima Bintou Rassoul Sy, Jesse James, and Liliana Coutinho.

The program was presented at FUSO Lisboa, at @museu_marioneta, and opened FUSO Insular at Igreja do Colégio in Ponta Delgada, inviting audiences on an audiovisual journey through artistic practices that explore the ecologies of relationships between humans and nonhumans, technology and spirituality, myth and the future.

𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝑩𝒆𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒊𝒏 𝑹𝒆𝒍𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏, ro heinrich, 2022, 10’24’’
The thought of Indigenous Brazilian leader Ailton Krenak and the voices of several interlocutors, including Erin Manning, open a meditative space on being as relation — a film that lingers in the trembling edges of difference, touch, and transformation.

𝑩𝒆𝒂𝒔𝒕𝑸𝒖𝒆𝒔𝒕, Kolbeinn Hugi, 2025, 30’ @animal.internet
Combines humour and science fiction to imagine a digital creature entering the ecological simulation GAIANET to configure a server for the Animal Internet — a techno-shamanic delirium where nature and cyberspace become interdependent.

𝑺𝒐𝒚 𝑴𝒖𝒄𝒉, Soya the Cow, 2021, 4’ @soyathecow
A queer, vegan pop manifesto celebrating freedom and the abundance of dissident bodies — human and non-human alike — through music, irony, and the assertion of difference.

|

In 2024, artist Tony Yap visited the West Coast to spend time in residence with The Unconformity. During this time, Tony and collaborator Jack Riley visited the Mt Lyell Mine with the support of Sibanye Stillwater, spent time in the unique West Coast landscape, and met with the local community, presenting work-in-progress developed during their stay.

Tony and Jack returned to Queenstown to perform Panjat Hujan at The Unconformity 2025 festival. Translating to 'Climbing the Rain', Panjat Hujan embodies the absence of the word 'impossible' from the language of indigenous Bugis people of South Sulawesi. Developed in response to their encounters on the West Coast, their performance explored symbolic rituals that refract time and space, bridging shamanistic tradition and contemporary dance to sold-out audiences.

Tony's 2024 residency was thanks to Asialink Arts at the University of Melbourne through the support of major partners Konfir Kabo and Monica Lim, The Yulgibar Foundation and Circle 5.

Image credit: Nick Hanson

[Image description: Three images of Tony and Jack performing Panjat Hujan. They are both wearing black and moving through an old hall, lit by bars of fluorescent lighting which sit diagonally throughout the space.]

In 2023, emerging visual artist Bridget Baskerville undertook a two week artist residency in Queenstown, thanks to the support of Arts Tasmania. Hailing from the regional mining town of Kandos in NSW, Bridget was particularly interested in bodies of water that have been impacted by human intervention, incorporating the agency of water in the mark-making process.

This year, Bridget returned to Queenstown to present her work Overflow at The Unconformity festival, working with local artist Iris Blazely. Suspended from the Queen River Footbridge, her kinetic sculpture work offered a gentle invitation to listen to the flow of water. Copper plates immersed in the Queen River were etched by acidic waters, transferring the traces of mining to new sensory mediums.

Image credit: Jesse Hunniford

[Image description: 1. A group of people crossing a footbridge over the Queen River, with long thin strips of copper hanging into the water below. 2. A close-up image of the copper strips sitting in the flowing orange waters of the Queen River. 3. A group of people standing on the riverbank observing the work. 4. A close-up image of Bridget's rusted orange metal work with unique markings. 5. A long roll of white paper, printed with orange lettering of a poem by Iris Blazely, hangs above a stack of rocks, rolling up towards the end 6. Thank you @yogadelmarspiritfestival for having me and capturing these beautiful moments. It was an honor to open the festival space…we began the weekend with a lunar eclipse and full moon in pisces with the theme: our dreams need a regulated body to land into. This is where we use a deep journey into sound to harmonize our biology and be receptive to the frequency and altitude of our highest selves. Pisces is the poet of the cosmos…a weekend where the stars remind us to step into the knowing of our inner eye and remember that collectively, we have no boundaries. We are one! Where instead of escaping into our dreams, we become enchanted by them and become the river to rush them into reality. 

We practice together so that our body, our container, is strong, rested and aligned to receive all of the magic and blessings that are continually on their way to us ✨🙏🏻 With this, the mantra that kept returning was one to cultivate our discernment between the real and the unreal … asatoma sad gamaya. 

If you’ve made it this far in my caption in the vast instagram world (hi, welcome, I am so glad you are here!), I invite you to close your eyes and chant this beautiful Pavamana Mantra. Chant when you are at a threshold, when you may be standing between what’s real and what’s illusion, when you may be beginning something new and when you may need to find your way back to clarity.

Om Asato Ma Sadgamaya
Tamaso Ma Jyotirgamaya
Mrityorma Amritam Gamaya
Om Shaanti, Shaanti, Shaanti
✨
Lead me from the unreal to the real
Move from illusion and untruth to eternal truth.
Lead me from darkness to light
Move from the ignorance of darkness to the light of wisdom.
Lead me from death to immortality
Move from mortal fear to the realization of the immortal self.
Om peace, peace, peace
Invoke ultimate peace within, around, and beyond.

Drawing from images collected over time across different Atlantic archipelagos, José Pedro Cortes explored impermanence, immersion, and silent observation. Through photography, he traced bodies and infrastructures in dialogue with a subterranean and volcanic cartography, where documentary recording met the poetic potency of an attentive gaze. His landscapes, portraits, and still lifes became visual maps of contemporary life — open, transitory, and unfinished. Joana Albuquerque’s sculptures extend this relationship between body and territory, evoke the shadows of resting bodies at Pesqueiro de Ponta Delgada, stretched out in the sun and water.

𝐉𝐨𝐬𝐞́ 𝐏𝐞𝐝𝐫𝐨 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐬 (@josepedrocortes) is a visual artist who works mainly with photography. His photographs – landscapes, portraits or still lifes – act as a map of visual possibilities that observe contemporary life. Through a personal, poetic and documentary form, his work mirrors a time of constant doubt in the construction of social relationships: impulse or fabrication, vulnerability or strength, the outer layer or something more.

𝐉𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐚 𝐀𝐥𝐛𝐮𝐪𝐮𝐞𝐫𝐪𝐮𝐞 (@joana___albuquerque) is based between Ponta Delgada and Munich. In her practice, through sculpture, objects and performances, she observes and analyses everyday gestures and social practices of her immediate surroundings. She is interested in the relation and interaction between the body and objects, power dynamics, and in the subversion of functionality. In her work there is an admiration for the pointless and things at rest.

After five extraordinary years with The Unconformity, last week we farewelled our outgoing Executive Producer, Maddie Korn.

Maddie’s leadership, care and tenacity have shaped some of our most ambitious festivals and explorations, strengthened our organisation, and deepened our connections across the West Coast and beyond. We’re grateful for her immense contribution and wish her every success in her next chapter.

We’re thrilled to welcome Jacqueline Dortmans as our new Executive Producer, commencing January 2026.

Jacqueline is a passionate arts leader and public administration professional with two decades of experience across major events, cultural organisations and creative projects. Her work spans Ten Days on the Island, Dark Mofo, MONA and the Tasmanian Government, and she recently served as creative lead on Jewelled Nights for The Unconformity 2025 program.

A musician, performer and advocate for accessible, community-centred arts, Jacqueline brings deep expertise in relationship-building, navigating complex arts and political landscapes, and championing Tasmanian stories and regional representation. We’re excited for the vision and energy she will bring to the West Coast.

Please join us in thanking Maddie for her incredible stewardship and in welcoming Jacqueline to The Unconformity team.

Monozukuri (ものづくり) levanta uma questão essencial: num mundo movido pela produção em massa, o que significa dedicar uma vida inteira ao aperfeiçoamento de um único ofício, como fazem muitos artesãos japoneses? No Japão, a arte de fazer coisas — monozukuri — é mais do que uma competência; é uma filosofia que honra a harmonia entre as mãos humanas, os materiais, a natureza e o tempo. Bilhetes na bio.

On September 12th, 2001, the day after the Twin Towers were attacked, street photographer Mike O’Meally captured the downtown New York landscape in a state of change. 9/12 features a trove of largely unseen photographs amidst a smoke-filled Lower Manhattan with sirens echoing around the crew. On black-and-white film, O’Meally captures skaters pushing through the streets shaped by loss—but buoyed by defiance in the wake of tragedy. To mark the 25th anniversary of September 11th, 2001, this new publication honours the spirit of New Yorkers who endured unimaginable hardship, yet persevered against all odds.

“Abundance is not something we acquire, it is something we tune into.”

𝐒𝐈𝐍𝐓𝐎𝐍𝐈𝐙𝐀𝐑 is to tune into something. To do so, two entities need to meet on the same frequency: one transmitting, the other receiving — and vice versa.

Curated by Rita Serra e Silva (@_rita_serraesilva) and Rita Westwood (@west_2_wood), the Public Programs of the Biennial 2025 invited everyone to explore 𝐺𝐸𝑆𝑇𝑈𝑅𝐸𝑆 𝑂𝐹 𝐴𝐵𝑈𝑁𝐷𝐴𝑁𝐶𝐸 over two months, through collective experiences that brought artists, communities, and visitors into closer connection with the island of São Miguel.

Across the Biennial, there were guided visits, creative workshops, a volunteering program, and excursions around the island inspired by the Biennial’s projects and open to the general public and school groups, among other activities.

|

“A abundância não é algo que adquirimos, é algo a que nos sintonizamos.”

Para o fazer, são necessárias duas entidades na mesma frequência: uma transmite, a outra recebe — e vice-versa.

Com curadoria de Rita Serra e Silva (@_rita_serraesilva) e Rita Westwood (@west_2_wood), os Programas Públicos da Bienal Walk&Talk 2025 convidaram a explorar 𝐺𝐸𝑆𝑇𝑂𝑆 𝐷𝐸 𝐴𝐵𝑈𝑁𝐷Â𝑁𝐶𝐼𝐴 durante dois meses através de experiências coletivas que aproximaram artistas, comunidades e visitantes da ilha de São Miguel.

Ao longo da Bienal, o programa desenvolveu-se através de visitas guiadas, oficinas criativas, um programa de voluntariado e excursões pela ilha inspiradas nos projetos da Bienal e abertas ao público em geral e a grupos escolares, entre outras atividades.

Nuno Pimenta designed and developed several of the spaces that housed Gestures of Abundance, including 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐚 𝐝𝐚 𝐁𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐥 — a space for information, resting, and informal encounters with the program.

On the ground floor of an abandoned building in the center of Ponta Delgada, Casa da Bienal was developed in collaboration with @spea_birdlife, an organization dedicated to restoring and preserving native ecosystems in the Azores. A living installation with native plants throughout the space, Casa da Bienal was composed of various spaces divided by curtains made from natural fibers: a multipurpose hall for film screenings, lectures, and gatherings.

𝐍𝐮𝐧𝐨 𝐏𝐢𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚 (@nunopimenta_) develops a transdisciplinary practice at the intersection of art and architecture. Working with a strategy of maximum economy of means, his practice draws on the subversion of traditional construction elements and techniques to create social, political, and ecological narratives.

|

Nuno Pimenta concebeu e desenvolveu vários dos espaços que acolheram Gestos de Abundância, entre eles a 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐚 𝐝𝐚 𝐁𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐥 — um espaço de informação, descanso e encontros informais com o programa.

No rés-do-chão de um edifício devoluto no centro de Ponta Delgada, a Casa da Bienal foi desenvolvida em colaboração com a SPEA – Sociedade Portuguesa para o Estudo das Aves, uma organização dedicada à recuperação e preservação dos ecossistemas nativos dos Açores. Em torno de uma instalação viva com plantas nativas pelo espaço, a Casa da Bienal organizou-se numa rede de espaços divididos por cortinas de fibras naturais: uma sala polivalente para projeções, palestras e encontros.

Earlier this year, The Unconformity offered a creative exploration based across Queenstown and Trial Harbour, on the West Coast of Lutruwita/Tasmania. The residency brought together local and visiting artists to explore site-specific collaboration, creative exchange, and the region’s layered landscapes–both social and physical.

Trial Harbour artist and studio host Jenny Groves welcomed the artists to the coast, with the group returning to Queenstown to share their work in an Open Hall event.

Bridie Hooper (QLD) and Jen Large (VIC/TAS) collaborated with West Coast artist David “Fitzy” Fitzpatrick, researching the intersection of circus, sculpture and performance art to explore effort, resilience and labour as cultural materials.

Polly Stanton (VIC) worked with Queenstown-based artist Jade Elford, combining video, sound and analogue photography to trace the shifting geographies and atmospheres of Queenstown and Trial Harbour.

Read more about the outcomes of this project on our website: theunconformity.com.au/coastal-collaboration

Meet the Judges

Homegrown may have been postponed to Sunday, but entries for Flotsam's surf clip and photography competitions slam shut at midnight tonight (Tues 19 May) to allow time for judging and notification of finalists. Here are just some of the leading figures across film and photography we're honoured to have on the 2026 judging panel: 

Christa Funk: @instaclamfunk one of the world’s leading surf and water photographers, renowned for capturing both the explosive power and quiet intimacy of life in the ocean. A former Coast Guard officer and lifelong competitive swimmer, Christa combined her passion for the water with photography to become a trailblazer in the surf world, making history as the first female water photographer to shoot during the Eddie Aikau Invitational. Now a respected presence at Pipeline and among surfing’s elite line-ups, her work is celebrated for its fearless water cinematography, storytelling depth and ability to document the world’s best surfers in moments both iconic and unseen.

Derek Hoffmann: @nalufilms a pioneering surf cinematographer and producer whose 30+ year career spans iconic 16mm water cinematography to prime-time television. Best known for groundbreaking work shooting from the water alongside Sonny Miller on classics including early The Search films including Searching for Tom Curren, as well as his film Fibreglass and Megapixels, Hoffmann is a six-time Emmy nominee through work on major television productions including Survivor and The Apprentice. Hoffman co-founded @nalufilms and later @nalufilmfoundation after the passing of Miller prompted action towards the protection, digitizing, and organizing of not just Miller’s footage in a database, but a pipeline of surfing’s most iconic filmmakers. 

Justin Gane: @pulsesurf pioneering Gold Coast surf filmmaker whose influential body of work helped define the Aussie surf film movement of the 1990s and beyond. A 30-year veteran of surf cinema, Gane rose to prominence with the cult classic Pulse, a landmark film credited with reshaping Aussie surf culture by spotlighting a generation of homegrown talent.

𝐑𝐄𝐕𝐈𝐒𝐈𝐓𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐖&𝐓’25
〰️ 𝐉𝐨𝐚𝐧𝐚 𝐒𝐚́, Variations on Unquietness (2025-ongoing)

Departing from the eruptive geology of the Azores, Variations on Unquietness listens to the planet as a restless body, exploring unquietness as a planetary, bodily, and relational condition — vibrational, tectonic, and imaginative.

Presented at Bienal Walk&Talk 2025, this performance-installation marked the first stage of a larger project developed by Joana Sá through field recordings, collaborative research, improvisation, and experimentation carried out during residencies in São Miguel (@walktalkazores) and Faial (@avistavulcao), and in response to the devastating 2025 wildfire in Serra da Estrela.

Bringing together sound, movement, light, and geological imagination, the work attunes itself to forces that often remain imperceptible — subterranean shifts, volcanic silence, and the resonances of ecological transformation inscribed upon bodies and territories.

🧶 𝐉𝐨𝐤𝐤𝐨𝐨 𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞, Spectral Traces (2025)

By combining field recordings, composition, film, and archival research, Jokkoo Collective’s installation invited us into a process of speculative investigation and deep listening. Inspired by cinematic dynamics and techniques used in sci-fi and horror, the ambiguous and affective power of sound took precedence over the visual, becoming the vital medium for drawing out traces of Afro-diasporic memories and resonances in the Azorean landscape.

𝐉𝐨𝐤𝐤𝐨𝐨 𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 (@jokkoo.collective) is a black multidisciplinary music collective based in Barcelona working from the intention and need to investigate and disseminate contemporary and futuristic creation of the experimental and alternative scenes of the African continent, its diaspora, and allied communities around the world.

|

Ao combinar gravações de campo, composição, vídeo e pesquisa de arquivo, a instalação de Jokkoo Collective convidou-nos a um processo de investigação especulativa e escuta profunda. Inspirada pela dinâmica cinematográfica e por técnicas utilizadas na ficção científica e no terror, o poder ambíguo e afetivo do som prevaleceu sobre o visual, tornando-se o meio vital para extrair vestígios de memórias e ressonâncias afro-diaspóricas na paisagem açoriana.

𝐉𝐨𝐤𝐤𝐨𝐨 é um coletivo multidisciplinar de música negra baseado em Barcelona, que trabalha com a intenção e a necessidade de investigar e divulgar as criações contemporâneas e futuristas das correntes experimentais e alternativas do continente africano, da sua diáspora e das suas comunidades aliadas em todo o mundo.

Flotsam Media + Makers was our annual festival meeting of minds, with panels sharing knowledge and insights into the world of creating media in the modern landscape across books and magazines to podcasts and film.

Hosted @bytimbaker and staring panels of leading creatives, it's a wonder the Kirra Hill hall didn't topple off it's hundred year old foundations under the sheer weight of knowledgeable grey matter onsite.

Panelist including Nick Carroll from @surfingworld and @weshouldntbefriends.pod Blake Johnson @blakeyjohnston Lauren L Hill @theseakin Katey Shearer @kateyshearer Tricia Shantz @neverlandthebook Todd Thimios @toddthimios Jamie Brooks @collectivedigital Stu Nettle @stunet and Kate McMahon @katemoments shared unfiltered views on everything from the rise of new media and AI, to the realities of freelancing and the ever-evolving world of print, film and broadcast.

By popular request, we'll be sharing recordings from these insightful sessions over on our Youtube channel very soon - watch this space. 

Blake's film In Pieces Together previewed after our panel on creating media with impact has since gone live - you can catch it free streaming on BINGE, Kayo and Fox Sports.

Flotsam Media + Makers is just one of the festival's commitment to skill building. Workshops, artist talks, Media + Makers projects and mentorship programs are delivered free and all access to build creative capacity across the region. The idea is simple: don’t just showcase culture, plant seeds to grow it.

🌼 𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐚 𝐌𝐚𝐥𝐯𝐚, Encantar lagoas: retomar lembranças, celebrar presenças (2025)

Following the traces of popular festivities, labour, traditions, and ways of life in Sete Cidades — one of the beating hearts of São Miguel — Encantar lagoas was a celebration of life in its passages and transformations. It honoured the lagoon as living organism, and the many beings who share, work, sing, create, and build their own culture and stories within a place that is as challenging as it is dazzling.

The first moment took the form of an installation at Arquipélago, serving as both precursor and invitation to a ritual actions that activated these objects during the Symposium weekend, culminating in a collective and participatory performance in Sete Cidades.

𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐚 𝐌𝐚𝐥𝐯𝐚 (@malva.colectiva) composed of 𝐄𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐧 𝐏𝐢𝐫𝐚́ 𝐖𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐮 and 𝐌𝐚𝐫/𝐭𝐚 𝐄𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐢𝐚̃𝐨, is a collective that conjoins, in a transdisciplinary way, research, curation, and artistic practices with the work of thinking, listening, and writing. 𝐄𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐧 𝐏𝐢𝐫𝐚́ 𝐖𝐚𝐬𝐬𝐮 (@ellenlimawassu) is an Indigenous artivist, poet, and researcher of Wassu Cocal origin. Her practice brings together performance, criticism, river bathing, conversations with flowers, and countercolonial thought. / 𝐌𝐚𝐫/𝐭𝐚 𝐄𝐬𝐩𝐢𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐢𝐚̃𝐨 (@martaespiridiao) is a non-binary curator, writer, and researcher invested in unearthing histories and erased ritual practices from the Iberian Peninsula, informed by intersectional feminist and queer thinking.

|

Seguindo os vestígios das festividades populares, do trabalho, das tradições e dos modos de vida nas Sete Cidades — um dos corações pulsantes de São Miguel — Encantar lagoas foi, acima de tudo, uma celebração da vida nas suas passagens e transformações. Homenageou este organismo vivo e os muitos seres que partilham, trabalham, cantam, criam e constroem a sua própria cultura e histórias dentro de uma geografia tão desafiadora quanto deslumbrante.

_

Fu*k fighting — it’s time to protect this blue heart of the sea.

We pushed big oil out. Now we’ve got a rare window to lock in World Heritage protection for the Great Australian Bight — before the next wave of extraction rolls in.

One of the last truly wild places on Earth. ~85% of species found nowhere else. Whales birthing. Sea lions resting. Ancient culture continuing. Waves pumping.

No leases. No rigs — thanks to you. Now we have a moment to act and protect this place forever.

This week is National Reconciliation Week 2026, and this morning at the National Reconciliation Week Breakfast in South Australia, the great Eddie Betts reminded us that "you cannot build a stable bridge from only one side of the river." 𝐔𝐡𝐮𝐫𝐚 𝐁𝐪𝐮𝐞𝐞𝐫 & 𝐒𝐨𝐲𝐚 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐰, Dedomestication (2025)

Bringing together drag, queer cosmologies, and decolonial thought, 𝐔𝐡𝐮𝐫𝐚 𝐁𝐪𝐮𝐞𝐞𝐫 & 𝐒𝐨𝐲𝐚 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐰 proposed Dedomestication as a gesture of poetic and political liberation. Through performance and installation, they dismantled boundaries between species and explored the body as a territory of resistance, desire, and reinvention — between the pop cow and the sacred jaguar, between ritual and protest.

In their recently premiered film, Dedomestication (BR/CH, 2026), a Swiss cow and an Amazonian panther meet for a drag queen adventure, full of questions about colonialism, climate change, animal rights and LGBTQIA+ activism.

𝐔𝐡𝐮𝐫𝐚 𝐁𝐪𝐮𝐞𝐞𝐫 (@uhurabqueer) is an Afro-Indigenous Brazilian artist and activist whose multidisciplinary practice is rooted in Black and Indigenous cosmologies, her work engages decolonial and queer ecologies, often focusing on the Amazon and anti-extractivist resistance. / 𝐒𝐨𝐲𝐚 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐰 (@soyathecow) is a Swiss drag cow, singer, and ecofeminist persona created by artist and activist Daniel Hellmann. Her performances blend pop, protest, and post-animal politics, interrogating species boundaries, love, and environmental collapse through satirical and poetic forms. Together, their collaboration forms a transcontinental alliance of queer ecopolitics and speculative activism.

|

🌬️ 𝐇𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐞 𝐒𝐢𝐥𝐣𝐞𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐦, Black Smokers (2025)

Black Smokers was a new creation within The Mountain Body series, Helle Siljeholm’s ongoing art and research project exploring mountains and geological formations as entangled more-than-human bodies across geological time and space. Inspired by volcanic vents unique to the Azores, the work began during the Opening Weekend, with a guided underwater immersion inviting participants to float and explore the sea with small driftwood sculptures gathered from across the archipelago. It was also accessible with a self-guided performance and installation at Centro Cultural da Caloura.

𝐇𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐞 𝐒𝐢𝐥𝐣𝐞𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐦 (@hellesiljeholm) is a choreographer and visual artist based in Oslo. Her practice crosses film, installation, sculpture, choreography and performance.

|

Black Smokers foi uma nova criação integrada na série The Mountain Body, o projeto artístico e de investigação de Helle Siljeholm, que explora montanhas e formações geológicas como corpos mais-do-que-humanos entrelaçados ao longo do tempo e do espaço geológicos. Inspirado nas fumarolas vulcânicas únicas dos Açores, começou durante o Fim de Semana de Abertura, com uma imersão subaquática orientada em que os participantes flutuaram e a exploraram o mar através de pequenas esculturas de madeira à deriva, recolhidas em diferentes pontos do arquipélago. Esteve também acessível como performance autoguiada durante toda a Bienal, no Centro Cultural da Caloura.

𝐇𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐞 𝐒𝐢𝐥𝐣𝐞𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐦 é coreógrafa e artista visual, baseada em Oslo. A sua prática involve cinema, instalação, escultura, coreografia e performance.

𝐒𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐚 𝐑𝐨𝐜𝐡𝐚, Buraco Azul (2025)

Buraco Azul extended Sofia Rocha’s research into ritual geologies and systems of listening to the earth. It created a threshold-space where stone and gesture became speculative language: an architecture of connection between visible and invisible, a place of transition, attention, and bodily listening. The work unfolded into graphic forms tattooed on the skin, expanding beyond the gallery as incorporated mineral memory and a shared gesture of abundance. In dialogue with clay pieces from the Municipal Museum of Vila Franca — vessels, containers, and incense burners — it established correspondences between local heritage, ancestral matter, and ritual imagination.

𝐒𝐨𝐟𝐢𝐚 𝐑𝐨𝐜𝐡𝐚 (@_s.sss.ss._ ) lives and works in Porto. An Azorean interdisciplinary visual artist who develops an artistic practice and research that seeks to approach invisible phenomena, flows and systems through material experimentation. Allegories, symbols and myths are transformed by various media, establishing speculative correspondences with three-dimensional forms, images and actions.
|

A instalação Buraco Azul prolongou a investigação de Sofia Rocha sobre geologias rituais e sistemas de escuta da terra. Criou um espaço-limiar onde pedra e gesto se tornaram linguagem especulativa: uma arquitetura de ligação entre visível e invisível, lugar de transição, de atenção e de escuta com o corpo. A obra desdobrou-se em formas gráficas tatuadas na pele, expandindo-se para além da galeria como memória mineral incorporada e gesto partilhado de abundância. Em diálogo com peças em barro do Museu Municipal de Vila Franca — vasos, recipientes e queimadores de incenso — estabeleceu correspondências entre património local, matéria ancestral e imaginário ritual.

🍊 𝐄𝐛𝐮𝐧 𝐒𝐨𝐝𝐢𝐩𝐨, The Way Her Teeth Settled (2025)

𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝒘𝒂𝒚 𝒉𝒆𝒓 𝒕𝒆𝒆𝒕𝒉 𝒔𝒆𝒕𝒕𝒍𝒆𝒅 dealt with erotics: of sound, sexual desire, violence, history, and names. We followed Vitoria, an enslaved trans woman kidnapped from Benin and brought to São Miguel in 1556, as she moved from an orange grove to her home to wash and finally to sleep. On the way, she had an erotic encounter with a stone and a client. Interceding this journey is a foray into the politics of the Western archive, collective memory, and the evolution of racialization. 

𝐄𝐛𝐮𝐧 𝐒𝐨𝐝𝐢𝐩𝐨 (@epastry) is a British-Nigerian artist and writer whose work spans performance, installation, video, and text. Her practice centers Black trans and queer experiences, speculating on futures by reimagining and reconstructing fragmented or erased histories. With an interdisciplinary and poetic approach, Sodipo engages archives — both official and intimate — through embodied storytelling, ritual, and research.

Smooth Cayenne Notes, a natural-dye textile installation, traces the global journeys of this pineapple variety since the 19th century, exploring its ecology and hidden bonds with other plants through color. Connecting the artist’s places of ancestry — Ghana and the Philippines — to the Azores, the work brings together one hundred textile squares, dyed with plants and soils, suspended inside an Azorean pineapple greenhouse. 
Using dye-baths from pineapple rinds and leaves on piña fiber, the installation generated a “plantone” catalogue mapping the plant’s entanglements with other species and territories. 

𝐌𝐚𝐞-𝐋𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐋𝐨𝐤𝐤𝐨 (@maelokko) is a professor at Yale University and works with agrowaste, ecological design and renewable biobased materials. She explores themes of generative justice by developing new models of distributed production and collaboration.

—

Smooth Cayenne Notes, uma instalação têxtil com tingimentos naturais, traça as viagens globais desta variedade de ananás desde o século XIX, explorando a sua ecologia e as ligações ocultas com outras plantas através da cor. Ligando os dois lugares de ancestralidade da artista — o Gana e as Filipinas — aos Açores, a obra reúne cerca de uma centena de quadrados têxteis, tingidos com plantas e solos, suspensos no interior de uma estufa de ananases açoriana.
Utilizando banhos de tingimento feitos a partir de cascas e folhas de ananás sobre fibra de piña, a instalação gerou um catálogo de “plantones” que mapeia os entrelaçamentos da planta com outras espécies e territórios.

(@culturgest @batalhacentrodecinema)

Sulphur Edges is a choreographic encounter shaped with and through place. Created during Forum Dança’s PACAP 8 / Mystery School residency in São Miguel, the 60-minute film unfolds across the island’s thermal sites, oceanfront pools, traces of a mine, and the shell of an abandoned hotel. These places act as co-agents in a process of sensing and transmission. Guided by Meg Stuart’s direction, the performers respond to the elemental conditions of each site. Movement arises from relation — to temperature, texture, invisible forces, and to one another. The camera moves as a choreographic partner, tracing tensions between body, place, and atmosphere. 

𝐌𝐞𝐠 𝐒𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭 is a choreographer, director and performer born in New Orleans and based in Berlin/Brussels, she is the founder of Damaged Goods and has created more than thirty productions that cross dance, theater and visual arts. Her work, centered on experimentation and the transformation of the body and the social, proposes dance as a space for rewriting narratives and bringing communities together. / Fórum Dança is a non-profit cultural association created in 1990 whose mission is to promote contemporary dance through professional and artistic training, research, publishing and documentation. Mystery School is an experimental program for performance artists, where composition, choreography and somatic practices intersect with mysticism, alchemy and curiosity about the invisible.

Many locals will recognise the sculpture ‘A Wave in Time’ on Emerson Street - a bronze moment capturing Sheila Williams walking her beloved dog, Raven. Sheila was the daughter of Ernest Williams, one of the notable architects of Napier’s post-earthquake rebuild.

Across the road a young boy, forever returning her greeting - a simple exchange that connects both sides of the street, and the past with the present.

The first sculpture was unveiled in 2010, with the young boy joining the story in 2014 - completing this beautiful tribute to the spirit of the 1930s.

Sheila Williams famously led the New Napier Week Carnival in January 1933, celebrating the city’s recovery following the devastating 1931 earthquake. She became a symbol of optimism, youth, and the bright future of a newly rebuilt Art Deco Napier.

From @art_deco_napier : Happy World Art Deco Day!

Celebrated on April 28, this day marks the opening of the iconic 1925 Exposition Internationale des Arts Décoratifs et Industriels Modernes in Paris, the event that gave rise to the Art Deco movement we know and love today.

Born from a desire to celebrate innovation, craftsmanship, and modern design, Art Deco continues to shape cities around the world, including right here in Napier.

And while the movement began in 1925, 1931 gave us some of the most breathtaking examples still admired today, from the Empire State Building to the Waldorf Astoria. Bold symbols of optimism and style during challenging times.

There’s no better place to celebrate than the Art Deco capital of the world.

Visit the Art Deco Trust and experience it for yourself:
Walking Tours: www.artdeconapier.com/walking-tours/
Vintage Car Tours: www.artdeconapier.com/car-tours/

Step back in time, soak up the stories, and see why this era still inspires today.
