At Fringe and beyond, if you spot a working dog out and about, here are a few friendly tips to keep in mind:
- Please don’t distract or pat a working guide or assistance dog
- Always speak to the handler, not the dog
- Under Australian law, they’re allowed anywhere the public can go, including public transport, shops and workplaces
- And yes… their favourite treats are carrots 🥕

Thanks for helping make Fringe (and beyond) a more accessible and welcoming space for everyone. 💛

𝐑𝐄𝐕𝐈𝐒𝐈𝐓𝐈𝐍𝐆 𝐖&𝐓’25
🪨 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐯𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞, The Gallivantation of the Promise (2025)

The Gallivantation of the Promise explored “wandering” as a method of knowledge and counter-cartography. Through intuitive and communal gestures, ephemeral scenographies, diasporic vocations, and ways of inhabiting territory were imagined with humor, precision, and relational radicality. 

𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐯𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 (@resolvecollective ) is an interdisciplinary group of designers, artists, and spatial practitioners based in the UK. Founded by Akil Scafe-Smith, Seth Scafe-Smith, and Gameli Ladzekpo, the collective operates at the intersection of architecture, social justice, and community organizing. Their practice focuses on using design as a tool for political engagement, often working with underrepresented communities to produce spatial interventions, exhibitions, and learning spaces that foster collective agency.

_

The Gallivantation of the Promise explorou o ato de “vaguear” como método de conhecimento e contra-cartografia. Através de gestos intuitivos e comunitários, imaginaram-se cenografias efémeras, vocações diaspóricas e formas de habitar o território com humor, precisão e radicalidade relacional. 

𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐯𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐯𝐞 (@resolvecollective) é um grupo interdisciplinar de designers, artistas e profissionais espaciais sediado no Reino Unido. Fundado por Akil Scafe-Smith, Seth Scafe-Smith e Gameli Ladzekpo, o coletivo opera na intersecção entre arquitetura, justiça social e organização comunitária. A sua prática centra-se na utilização do design como ferramenta de envolvimento político, trabalhando frequentemente com comunidades sub-representadas para produzir intervenções espaciais, exposições e espaços de aprendizagem que promovem a ação coletiva.

—

📹 Bernardo Bordalo, @claudiodustd, @rui.no @marianalidl @joaopedrocosta.pt

Artist Emma Bugg invites you to participate in Elemental Memories, a creative workshop that explores the stories and connections we hold in everyday objects.

Young people are encouraged to BYOO (Bring Your Own Object) to transform into a special charm that will become part of a larger artwork.

Don’t worry if you don’t have one; spare objects will be provided.

Please note: Any objects you bring will be donated to the project and become part of its ongoing story.

Day 8 | Mais uma noite inesquecível no Portuguese Surf Film Festival. 💙

Ontem celebrámos o Women in Surf Films com casa cheia, um ambiente inspirador e momentos que ficarão na memória de todos.

O Welcome Drink by @dear.rose.cafe foi delicioso, a música da @loisdsldp emocionou e contagiou a sala, e o Meet & Greet da Ocean Art Gallery foi um verdadeiro sucesso, proporcionando momentos especiais entre artistas, realizadoras e o público.

Tivemos mulheres incríveis em palco a partilhar as suas histórias, os seus negócios e mensagens verdadeiramente inspiradoras.

Identificar uma necessidade, acreditar numa ideia e transformá-la num projeto é um enorme ato de coragem. Foi exatamente assim que nasceu a @swella.app , a app idealizada e desenvolvida pela Rita, criada por uma mulher a pensar nas necessidades de tantas outras mulheres. Histórias como esta lembram-nos da importância de dar voz a quem inspira, cria e abre caminho.

Foram quatro os filmes da noite que celebraram em grande as histórias de mulheres, feitos por mulheres. Parabéns às realizadoras de She in Storms, Cold Water Sirens, Wahine Waveriders e Guts.

Ficámos absolutamente deliciados com todas as mensagens e comentários que recebemos das muitas mulheres que estiveram presentes nas sessões de ontem. Continuem a partilhar connosco as vossas opiniões. Keep ’em coming! 💙

Muito obrigada a todos os que estiveram presentes e fizeram parte desta noite tão especial. Um agradecimento muito especial aos nossos parceiros @flord.estufa e @quintadacerca.restaurante por todo o apoio ao longo destes anos, e à Câmara Municipal de Mafra @camara_municipal_mafra , por tornar possível trazer o Portuguese Surf Film Festival até todos nós.

E um enorme obrigada à nossa equipa: Susana, Fernanda, Alice, Bibiana, Isabel, Elisabete e Cândida. Por toda a dedicação, paixão e trabalho incansável para tornar cada detalhe desta noite uma realidade. Nada disto seria possível sem vocês 🫶🏻

Happy World Art Deco Day!

Celebrated on April 28, this day marks the opening of the iconic 1925 Exposition Internationale des Arts Décoratifs et Industriels Modernes in Paris, the event that gave rise to the Art Deco movement we know and love today.

Born from a desire to celebrate innovation, craftsmanship, and modern design, Art Deco continues to shape cities around the world, including right here in Napier.

And while the movement began in 1925, 1931 gave us some of the most breathtaking examples still admired today, from the Empire State Building to the Waldorf Astoria. Bold symbols of optimism and style during challenging times.

There’s no better place to celebrate than the Art Deco capital of the world.

Visit the Art Deco Trust and experience it for yourself:
Walking Tours: www.artdeconapier.com/walking-tours/
Vintage Car Tours: www.artdeconapier.com/car-tours/

Step back in time, soak up the stories, and see why this era still inspires today.

Some people arrive knowing exactly what they’re looking for.

Most don’t.

And that’s often when the best discoveries happen.

From gin tastings on a river cruise in the city, to immersive experiences in Whyalla, to guided tours at Nilpena Ediacara National Park, there’s still plenty happening across metro and regional SA. And yes, there’s even a virtual show you can catch from your couch 👀

Keep the party going!!

If you’ve had a sauna with us previously - did you notice a difference? 

We recently upgraded our wood heater to a high stone-mass Finnish heater with a whopping 400kg of stones, and it’s changed the feel of Kuuma in a subtle but beautiful way.

Our IKI heater is designed to run with slightly lower room temperatures, but with much greater depth of heat and steam (löyly). The result is a softer, more enveloping experience that builds slowly and warms deep into your core, rather than hitting hard and intense all at once.

If you think of traditional saunas being hot, dry, and fast, like a flame-grilled steak — IKI is something a bit different.

Lower, deeper, unhurried heat. 
A bit more like slow-cooked brisket… 

Both have their place in the world. 
But at Kuuma, we like to lean into the deep, immersive and everlasting side of the experience, and IKI does that perfectly…

Kuuma 🌊

The road to Queenstown is no small undertaking.

Winding through Lutruwita/Tasmania’s rugged and mountainous West Coast, the journey can take up to four hours – past lakes, forests and old mining towns, with long stretches where mobile reception falls away.

For most festival-goers, this drive is part of The Unconformity experience. But it’s also a road that demands care and attention.

That’s why this year, we’re launching our Safe Journeys Campaign with the Road Safety Advisory Council, encouraging everyone to slow down, plan ahead and travel mindfully.

To help you stay alert, you can grab a coffee on us – just mention you’re heading to The Unconformity at Hungry Wombat Café at Derwent Bridge or Big Z Café in Zeehan. This offer is available until Monday 20 October.

Take your time, schedule breaks, and enjoy the journey–it’s all part of the festival.

Video credit: Lusy Productions

WILDERNESS — ARCTIC EDITION ❄️🔥

Immersion into the cold stillness of the North.

Snow settling 
Water freezing 
Wind moving across ice.

🌅 𝐂𝐀𝐑𝐀 𝐋𝐀𝐕𝐀𝐃𝐀, Geoteluric Orisons (2025)

Geoteluric Orisons was a contemporary reflection on the significance of being Azorean, the relationship between memory, identity, and territory, and the ability to project new narratives of abundance, participation, and belonging. With an 𝑒𝑥ℎ𝑖𝑏𝑖𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛, 𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑠, 𝑖𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠, and a 𝑑𝑖𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑟-𝑖𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛, 𝐂𝐀𝐑𝐀 𝐋𝐀𝐕𝐀𝐃𝐀's program built a system of connections between contemporary art, local cultural expressions, gastronomy, and landscape.

This project was selected for the Programming Open Call, aimed at independent collectives and cultural spaces based in São Miguel. This initiative supports and gives visibility to new artistic proposals, diversifying the Biennial’s program and strengthening the network of local cultural agents.

𝐂𝐀𝐑𝐀 𝐋𝐀𝐕𝐀𝐃𝐀 (@we.are.caralavada) is a young collective of intervention, creation and artistic production, interdisciplinary, experimental and contumacious from the city of Ponta Delgada. Its practices explore the limits of collective socio-political realities, starting from common places and identity.

Geoteluric Orisons foi uma reflexão contemporânea sobre a Açorianidade, a relação entre memória, identidade e território, e a capacidade de projetar novas narrativas de abundância, participação e pertença. Why is the water so green?

That glowing emerald colour is a sign of a healthy bay. In the warmer months, the seagrass meadows of North West Bay flourish beneath the surface, reflecting sunlight into a brilliant green colour. At the same time it naturally filters the water and captures carbon — keeping the bay clear, vibrant and alive.

Some say it’s nature’s own filtration system — growing and glowing, right beneath Kuuma, but we just like to think that a sunny day is when she likes to show off her sparkly green dress… 

Book a trip with us and you too can swim in a sea of nature’s glittering green gemstones…

𝑬𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒅𝒐 𝒅𝒆 𝑮𝒓𝒂𝒄̧𝒂 is a continuous project and tribute to the land and territory, its products, and to those who care for it, transform it, and share it. Focusing on the Mercado da Graça in Ponta Delgada — a space of crossings, a meeting point, and a living expression of the territory of São Miguel — where colors, textures, aromas, flavors, and stories reveal the richness of the island in multiple layers and intersections. During the Biennial, the project proposed moments of activation and participation: an exhibition, a market stall, talks, and guided visits, celebrating the connections between products, producers, vendors, and consumers, while promoting conscious consumption, encounter, sustainability, and quality food. The 𝐸𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑑𝑜 𝑑𝑒 𝐺𝑟𝑎𝑐̧𝑎 𝑆𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑙 presented proposals inspired by the market and autumn harvests; the exhibition P𝑃𝑟𝑎𝑐̧𝑎 𝑑𝑎 𝐺𝑟𝑎𝑐̧𝑎 highlighted the stories and vitality of this place; and the cycle concludes with a 𝑆𝑜𝑝𝑎 𝑑𝑎 𝑃𝑒𝑑𝑟𝑎, a communal meal marking both an ending and the beginning of a new time. At the end of the cycle, the 𝑀𝑎𝑟𝑘𝑒𝑡 𝑇𝑎𝑙𝑘𝑠 brought together people from various fields for a discussion on the history and sustainability of local agriculture.

📡 𝐋𝐮𝐜𝐲 𝐁𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡, An Infrasonorous Archipelago (2025)

An Infrasonorous Archipelago investigates the vibrational kinships between the antipodean archipelagos of Tasmania and the Azores. In collaboration with IVAR – Instituto de Investigação em Vulcanologia e Avaliação de Riscos — and Professor Nicolau Wallenstein, the artist collected and translated infrasonic data (low-frequency seismic waves) into a suite of poetic and tactile works. Using a series of propositions explored through experimental drawing, video, sculpture and performance, the artist reflected on the value of the incidental, of reciprocity, and of what is felt (more than known).

𝐋𝐮𝐜𝐲 𝐁𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 is an artist based in lutruwita/Tasmania whose practice explores geologic volatility, material transformation, and deep time. Working through site-responsive installations, drawing, and collaborative fieldwork, her projects often engage with local communities, scientists, and natural forces to investigate the poetics of instability and environmental entanglement.

Art Deco Trust Inc is a not-for-profit registered charity CC21328 formed by a passionate group of individuals in 1985 to voice their opposition to the demolition of a number of Napier’s iconic art deco era buildings.

The Trust’s mission and purpose is to protect, promote and celebrate our art deco era heritage and we are the guardians, storytellers, and interpreters of the regions art deco era heritage following the devastating 1931 Hawke’s Bay earthquake. 

Our protection, promotion and celebration of the city’s heritage bring vibrancy to the city of Napier, generates tourism, economic prosperity, and engenders community pride and identity. 

We do this by hosting walking and vintage car tours of the city of Napier; we provide heritage advisory services and provide grants to building owners for the maintenance of their buildings through the Robert McGregor Heritage Fund; we host the biannual Hawke’s Bay Heritage Awards; and we celebrate our city’s heritage annual by hosting the iconic Art Deco Festival Napier.

The Trust is generously supported by our community of art deco friends and supporters who enable us to ensure the spirit of Art Deco shines on!

On the last day of the Biennial, this chapter of Maria Emanuel Albergaria’s project 𝑬𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒅𝒐 𝒅𝒆 𝑮𝒓𝒂𝒄̧𝒂 ended with a community soup prepared using products from the market, in a moment gathering vendors and visitors.

Later that afternoon, Haseeb Iqbal told us stories of the origins of sound system culture in 1940s Jamaica and beyond, using Walk&Talk’s own sound system to share some of the music that was being played on these DIY systems through the decades. 

At Casa da Bienal, Beatrice Leanza presented her book 𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝑵𝒆𝒘 𝑫𝒆𝒔𝒊𝒈𝒏 𝑴𝒖𝒔𝒆𝒖𝒎, that maps a new landscape of institutional practices across different geographical locations, including Walk&Talk in Sao Miguel, as alternative educational and collaborative frameworks of institutional development.

A roaming robotic nun that revives the life and legacy of Madre Margarida do Apocalipse, a cloistered Azorean nun and creator of the Arcano Místico — an extraordinary and mystical work composed of over 10,000 small figurines made from bread, resin, seashells, and natural pigments found on the island. Alice reimagines this figure as a symbol of resistance and emotional expression, proposing a speculative cosmology that combines themes of childhood, make-believe, and mythic soothsaying.

𝐀𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐕𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧 (@alice.visentin) is an Italian artist who explores reality as a mutable dimension, transformed by interactions between bodies and words, dreams and murmurs. Through her work, she investigates the generative capacity of imagination and the possibility of accessing other levels of perception and experience, guided by an intuitive understanding of things facilitated by her encounters with others.

_

Uma freira robótica errante que revive a vida e o legado de Madre Margarida do Apocalipse, freira açoriana enclausurada e criadora do Arcano Místico — uma obra extraordinária e mística composta por mais de 10.000 pequenas figuras feitas de pão, resina, conchas e pigmentos naturais encontrados na ilha. Alice reimagina esta figura como um símbolo de resistência e de expressão emocional, propondo uma cosmologia especulativa que combina temas de infância, faz-de-conta e adivinhação mítica.

𝐀𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐕𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧 é uma artista italiana que explora a realidade como uma dimensão mutável, transformada pelas interações entre corpos e palavras, sonhos e murmúrios. 🧶 𝐖𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐚 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐛𝐨, To Burn the Grids Away (2025)

Earth’s time cannot be mastered, and along the borders once drawn to dominate territories, many were born who were meant to breathe freedom. 𝐖𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐚 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐛𝐨’s speculative installation sowed into the imagination the promise of one day awakening by the volcanoes that refused to be mastered. If iron rusts and returns to ore, the day will come when the earth’s abundance returns and the monocultures become forests once again. The artist proposed, through the installation, an interweaving of Afro-diasporic spiritual practices with Azorean communal cosmologies and quilombos imaginaries.

𝐖𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐚 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐛𝐨 (@wallacapelobo), invited to be part of the Biennial through the Open Call for Artists, is a Brazilian artist and researcher working across sculpture, installation, writing, and performance. Her practice explores Afro-diasporic futurisms, land-based spiritualities, and speculative ecologies. Engaging with both popular and esoteric visual languages, she reimagines ritual, resistance, and community care through embodied, often collaborative gestures.

|

O tempo da Terra não pode ser dominado, e é junto às fronteiras que outrora tentaram subjugar territórios que nasceram muitos daqueles destinados a respirar liberdade. A instalação especulativa de 𝐖𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐚 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐛𝐨 semeou no imaginário a promessa de um dia despertar junto aos vulcões que se recusaram a ser dominados. Se o ferro enferruja e regressa a minério, chegará o dia em que a abundância da terra retornará e as monoculturas voltarão a ser florestas. A artista propôs, através da instalação, um entrelaçamento de práticas espirituais afro-diaspóricas com cosmologias comunitárias açorianas e imaginários de quilombos.

—

Este é o terceiro espaço que acolhe as criações dos jovens artistas Micaelenses, após o @parque.atlantico e o Museu Municipal da Ribeira Grande.

Ao longo de seis meses, seis jovens de São Miguel — Inês Amorim, Júlia Craveiro, Júlia Rego, Martim Teixeira, Pilar Farias e Sara Almeida — refletiram criativamente sobre a importância de viver segundo lógicas de abundância, explorando diferentes técnicas artísticas e desenvolvendo projetos com o apoio de André Laranjinha e da equipa do 𝑆𝐼𝑁𝑇𝑂𝑁𝐼𝑍𝐴𝑅 – Programas Públicos da Bienal Walk&Talk. .

📍 Casa João de Melo (Achadinha), Nordeste

The 𝑫𝑬𝑺𝑪𝑶𝑳𝑨 exhibition opened last friday, 6.02, at Casa João de Melo, in Nordeste, continuing its itenerary through the island. This is already the third space welcoming the creations of the young artists from São miguel, after Parque Atlântico and Museu Municipal da Ribeira Grande.

Over six months, six young people from São Miguel — Inês Amorim, Júlia Craveiro, Júlia Rego, Martim Teixeira, Pilar Farias, and Sara Almeida — creatively reflected on the importance of living according to logics of abundance, exploring different artistic techniques and developing projects with the support of André Laranjinha and the 𝑆𝐼𝑁𝑇𝑂𝑁𝐼𝑍𝐴𝑅 team.

Despite weeks of rain, soggy grounds and morning showers, the Mullumbimby Community Market still came alive today.

The band may have packed down early, but a beautiful core of stallholders stayed on with optimism, warmth and big smiles. The Maypole dance went ahead, the sun eventually arrived, buskers gathered and sang to us, and people lingered over coffee, vintage treasures and good conversations.

A huge thank you to the girls who stayed behind helping untangle the Maypole ribbons, to the musicians and buskers who kept the atmosphere alive, to our dedicated stallholders who showed up through uncertain weather, and to every visitor who came out to support local.

Days like today remind us what community really is.

Thank you, Mullum. 🌿

TOMORROW May 13, join surfer/shaper/artist/photographer @harveysurf for the Wish You Were Here exhibition + talk story

Step into a time before Instagram, when a single postcard image was the FOMO mechanism to spark wanderlust and put the Gold Coast on traveler’s itinerary.

Wish You Were Here is Richard Harvey's curated exhibition bringing together his personal collection of vintage postcards and his own postcard-perfect photographs.

Commissioned to shoot postcard images in his early years, Harvey’s lifelong fascination with visual storytelling began. Wish You Were Here traces that journey, from faded, found relics of early Gold Coast life to striking scenes captured through his own lens, the collection reveals how surf culture, travel, and image-making have always been intertwined.

An iconic figure in Australian surf, Harvey’s story runs parallel to the evolution of the coast itself; from his early days competing on the world stage, shaping boards on the Gold Coast, and documenting Queensland’s surfing heritage. 

The talk story evening will see Richard sharing firsthand insights into how postcard imagery once fueled tourism, the shifting identity of the Gold Coast, and why these small, tangible images mattered long before the digital age.

Exhibition: until 15 May @coolangattasandshotel 

Talk Story: 13 May, 6:00 pm - Free

PLACES YOU DON’T WANT TO MISS IN TASMANIA
PART 21 🔥🌊
Kuuma Nature Sauna

Kuuma Nature Sauna honestly lived up to every bit of the hype. A wood fired sauna on a pontoon boat, cruising out to a quiet bay before anchoring up and turning into the dreamiest floating sauna session.

You book a 1.5 hour session, either shared with others or private. Once anchored, the gate opens and it becomes your swimming platform. Sauna, fresh air, repeat.

Then comes the cold part. Jump straight into the water or use the classic bucket shower if you’re easing into it. Cold water sits around 9° in winter and 17° in summer and somehow you keep going back for more.

We went in the morning and it was next level. Calm, peaceful, and the perfect reset. There is no better way to start your day!

Are you a Sauna fan?

✨ Save this for your Tasmanian bucket list!

LET THE CHILDREN LEAD ❤️‍🔥

Last night in Mallorca, these two little legends ended up jamming with me for almost half my entire set 😂🥁

And I loved every second of it.

We talk so much about children being the leaders of the future…

But I believe they are our leaders NOW.

They are our gurus. 🧘🏽

They arrive so close to innocence. So close to wonder. So close to God.

Before the conditioning.
Before worrying what everyone thinks.
Before being told how they’re supposed to move, sing, dress, dream or express themselves.

They just ARE.

Maybe our responsibility isn’t always to teach them how to become more like us.

Maybe it’s to protect their innocence, create safe spaces for them to flourish, and occasionally have the humility to get out of the way and let them remind us how to live.

Last night, I wasn’t interested in getting these kids off my stage.

I wanted to follow them 😂❤️‍🔥

More children on dance floors.
More children on stages.
More intergenerational community.
More spaces where the whole family gets to belong.

The children are already leading.

Are we listening? 🌍❤️

This is why we’re all in. Stunning words from one of our community members who experienced Karla Bidi this past Festival. 

Created by First Nations artists Ilona McGuire, Jacob Nash, Chloe Ogilvie and Ian Moopa Wilkes, under the guidance of Noongar Elders including Vivienne 'Binyarn' Hansen, 'Karla Bidi' is a powerful and poetic installation transforming the Derbarl Yerrigan/Swan River and Djarlgarro/Canning River into a glowing pathway of 11 beacons stretching from Walyalup to Mandoon. 

The photos and reflection above is about our Kaarta Gar-Up Lookout site in Kings Park. A vital meeting place, ceremonial ground, and source of identity, providing traditional custodians with shelter, bush medicine, and sustenance.

Portland Sunday Parkways Presented by @kpnorthwest returns to East Portland this Sunday, June 28, from 11 a.m.–4 p.m.! 
 
Join PBOT and explore 4 miles of car-free streets connecting Ventura Park, Lincoln Park, Parklane Park, and our newest addition to this event route, Verdell Burdine Rutherford Park. Enjoy vendor marketplaces, live entertainment, and family-friendly activities as you walk, bike, roll, and play in the streets at this free community event.  
 
Coming from Gresham? Join the @cityofgresham Bike Bus departing from Gresham City Hall at 11 a.m. and ride to the event with experienced ride leaders. 
 
Highlights include: 
• Free Portland Rides e-bike demos and rebate information  
• Adaptive Bike Clinic and adaptive group ride hosted by Adaptive BIKETOWN, Adaptive Sports Northwest, and Shriners Children’s Portland  
• City of Gresham bike obstacle course and bike-powered smoothie blender  
• Free skateboarding lessons with @dreambig.pdx, including free skateboard rentals and safety gear  
• Live music and performances throughout the route, including DJ Ambush, Majik9, Hip Hop Soulsation Academy, Hall and Oakes, The Bylines, My Voice Music, and Chrissy Marie.  
• Learn how to Fix a Flat with PBOT’s Portland By Cycle team 
• Roller disco party with DJ Doc Rock and free roller skate rentals for all ages from Rose City Rollers 
 
Streets along the route will be closed to motorized traffic from 9 a.m.–5 p.m. with limited local access. Volunteers and temporary barricades will be stationed at intersections to help guide drivers through the area. No parking is allowed on the route, and vehicles left in posted areas will be ticketed and towed beginning at 6 a.m.

Mathew Tildesley (@mat_tildesley) works as a skipper on the tourist boats that ply the waters of the Freycinet Peninsula off Tasmania’s east coast. But for the past decade, he has also been working on a singular artistic project: using a waterproof flash to photograph beautiful waves breaking a kilometre offshore at night.⁠
⁠
His Surf Strobe project started as a “wacky idea,” but now, it’s his passion. It reveals “all these amazing textures and little details that you would never see," and it's exhibiting now at the Flotsam Film and Photo Festival (@flotsam.festival) on the Gold Coast. ⁠

Good news story! Jaha Koo, creator of the wonderful work ‘Haribo Kimchi’ (Perth Festival 2026) has won the International Ibsen Award for ‘his innovative and deeply human theatre.’ 💛

This prestigious award is the world’s largest theatre prize and often referred to as the Nobel Prize of theatre.

'The theatre he creates is quiet, yet deeply political. It cuts through ideological noise and speaks directly to our shared human experience,' says Ingrid Lorentzen, chair of the jury for the International Ibsen Award and artistic director of the Norwegian National Ballet. 

We’re so happy we were able to bring Koo’s incredible work to Perth audiences!

I’ve got lots more to say when I’m done at my “real” job, but I wanted to share a little bit of gratitude for all of the volunteers who come together to make Bike Summer happen. 

Just a few weeks ago my main cargo bike was stolen. This morning my back-up cargo bike “died.” All I had left to haul all of our Bike Summer gear and merch was one old Bianchi bike with a massive Wald basket. But then there was ZANE with his incredible long haul trailer (and his rad stories) who was willing to bike all the way across town (SE to NE) to meet me, load up, pedal downtown to unload, and then bike to SE to deliver the remaining merch. And he wouldn’t even accept lunch as a “Thank you”.

“What gets you downtown these days (aside from hauling Bike Summer gear), Zane?” “The farmers markets.”
… ”But that’s as a volunteer to collect donations for Food Not Bombs, right?” “Yeah.”

The vast majority of Bike Summer rides are hosted by volunteers. The lions share of the events are free. And the community comes out to enjoy and support in amazing ways as corkers, medics, co-leaders, photographers, haulers of sound systems, cup cake makers, and happy participants. This Instagram account is managed by volunteers. The calendar we use is open source and developed by volunteers (thank you, @shift2bikes!!). Our non profit board is volunteer run (we love you, Umbrella!). And the community grows every year.

Yes, it’s a whole heck of a lot of work to make bike fun happen, but it’s a JOY to do it. THANK YOU for making rides happen and THANK YOU for coming out on a Monday to ride and even on a hot Tuesday morning to volunteer.  Back to work. Hope to see you on the streets,

- Meghan

P.S. Last summer we had a handful of really wonderful people pitch in on social media, but it was @evafrazier who really kept things rolling with her weekly round ups. This summer @ryanlacher has come on to support with weekly posts, too. We cannot wait for y’all to meet her!

P.P.S. With some coaxing Zane took a pennant as a small token of appreciation, and with great delight we saw a little bit of him in the raccoon design. 🦝 🦺 🚲

3.55pm Future of Media
Surf media once meant magazines and movies, but with print in decline and social media prompting snack-sized content, what is surf media? A panel dissects surf forecasting sites, AI, vloggers, and influencers and consumer trends.

Day one, and already... everything shifted.

We began in stillness. A circle, a ceremony, breath before words.
Then the bowls sang, and the noise we didn’t know we were carrying began to lift.

We begin to let go.

Of expectations. Of heaviness. Of everything but the moment we are in.

And in that lightness, we find simplicity.

Live music that feeds something deeper than simply the pleasure of the ears.

As the sun dropped behind the mountains, and our ECLIPSE lit up, the energy shifted with it. From stillness to celebration.

Lights, movement, bodies free.
Because in the end, it was never about the noise around us.

It’s the peace we carry inside.

And that was only day one.

This is not a brand activation. 
Before influencers and 3-second attention spans, surf films were a slow art built for big screens. 

Flotsam: Retrospect
5.30PM, May 3, Kirra Hill Cultural Centre - one night only

As the sun sets over Kirra, pay homage to MP overlooking his old stomping grounds with Searching for Michael Peterson- a tribute to one of surfing’s most enigmatic icons.
Then, on the eve of the 50th anniversary of Tubular Swells, join surf film pioneer Dick Hoole, surfer Richard Harvey and a cast of luminaries for a rare panel unpacking the craft, culture and legacy of surf filmmaking.. and the impact of local stars like MP on screen.

Then shuttle into a time capsule of Australian surf culture with You Should Have Been Here Yesterday. A poetic homage built from hundreds of hours of lovingly restored 16mm footage, set to a salt-infused soundtrack by Headland and featuring visionaries including Tim Winton, Wayne Lynch, Bob McTavish, Albe Falzon, Evelyn Rich and Maurice Cole.

Join us for an evening of unearthed reels, original soundscapes and a cinematic drift through the wild, formative era of surf culture. Tix in bio!

This May 1-15, 2026, annual surf festival Flotsam turns its focus firmly to home, unveiling a powerful program of exhibitions and events that celebrate the Gold Coast’s rich surf culture, visual history and creative community all set against the coastline that inspired it.

At the heart of the program, Icons transforms the exterior of The Pink Hotel into a striking open-air gallery. Through large-scale black-and-white photography, the exhibition captures a coastline in transition – from lost landmarks to enduring surf breaks – offering a raw, unfiltered tribute to the people and places that define the region. Each image connects to deeper stories via QR codes, linking you to the stories behind each frame. Launching May 6 with rooftop drinks and a film night at Eddie’s Bar, Icons is both a celebration and a time capsule of the Gold Coast’s evolving identity.

A passionate obsession born through the desire to see world class unrideable swells potentially ridden deep in the cold unpredictable Australian rugged coastline.

"I moved from the inner city comfort of South Australia, jumped the border and set my sites on the heavy barreling waters of Western Australia. Not content with my content fuels the ambitions to seek greater images with articulated awareness that the potential for undesirable outcomes are inevitable."
~ Trent Slater

International Masters of Surf is a carefully curated gathering of the world’s most influential surf photographers, whose work has helped shape surfing’s visual history.

@nickgreenphoto : Introducing Nick Green to Flotsam's 2026 International Masters of Surf roll call, one of the brand new inductees joining the 50+ luminaries already featured in this landmark exhibition. 

Growing up in Tasmania, Australia, Nick has spent decades focused on the Southern Ocean and its surf coastlines.

"My work explores the relationship between people and wild ocean environments shaped by exposure, isolation and weather.

Working primarily in black and white, I’m drawn to the rawness and timelessness of these places, documenting waves, coastlines and the quiet human presence that exists alongside them. Surfing forms part of a broader connection to the coastline here, where access, environment, isolation, and changing conditions shape the experience as much as the waves themselves.,"

Alongside this long-term personal work, Nick has published long-form stories through international platforms focused on ocean culture, environment and place-based storytelling.

International Masters of Surf is a curated gathering of the world’s most influential surf photographers, whose work has helped shape surfing’s visual history. 

Catch Nick's submission to Flotsam’s International Masters of Surf when the exhibition returns in May at @dust_temple

🔔✨ Veronica Bell Ceremony – Art Deco Festival Napier ✨🔔

📅 Date: Sunday, 22 February 2026
🕛 Time: 12:00 pm – 12:30 pm
📍 Location: Veronica Sun Bay, Marine Parade, Napier
🎟 Cost: Free

A Moment of Commemoration. We gather with the Acting Dean of the Anglican Cathedral, the Westshore Sea Scouts, and members from the Napier Pipe Band, to honour the memory of the 1931 earthquake — one of New Zealand’s greatest natural disasters. At the heart of the ceremony stands the Veronica Bell, a lasting symbol of both tragedy and strength. Gifted in recognition of the Navy’s tireless efforts in the aftermath, it continues to be rung as a reminder of resilience, compassion, and community. As we remember those who lost their lives, we also give thanks for the enduring spirit that carried Hawke’s Bay forward in the face of devastation. The ceremony concludes with the Veronica Bell escorted to the Cathedral by a bagpiper and drummer from the Napier Pipe Band.

Music, Magic & High Vibes at Yoga del Mar Spirit Festival ✨

27–30 August · Only Summer Finca, Llubí, Mallorca

Yoga del Mar Spirit Festival is much more than a yoga festival. Music is at the heart of the experience, with live concerts, Ecstatic Dance, DJ sets, Kirtans and live acoustic music woven throughout the four festival days.

Evening highlights ✨✨

Thursday: Kirtan Ibiza with Beatrice & Hector Koa open the festival, followed by a live DJ set from Mallorcan DJ Paco Colombàs.

Friday: Franko Heke brings a Cosmic Kirtan, followed by J-Pool with a tribal hybrid dance set.

Saturday: Franko Heke returns with a Future Mantra electronic set, followed by Dani Bogari from Saudi Arabia with a high-vibe Ecstatic Dance set.

Sunday: Hanuman Project closes the festival with a beautiful Kirtan & cacao experience by Kakaochi. 

And the music continues throughout the days: David Lurey offers Kirtan, Juan from Ibiza plays live guitar during Friday and Saturday lunch, SetSun from Mallorca bring handpan & guitar sessions at dinner, and Pao Pamaki shares a Medicine Music concert.

Come for the full four days, for the weekend, for one day or for the evening concert only (30-35€ & free parking from 6pm onwards) - All tickets are now available

Come early, wander through the artisan and food market, enjoy healthy food and drinks, discover local handmade products, and soak up the festival atmosphere. Then gather in community circle before transitioning into the evening concerts and dance.

Kingdom Of The Evening by @clint__davis 
Surfer Kepa Acero reconnects with his past on a surf trip through Morocco 

Haus Tumbuna by @matty_hannon 
- a documentary film set in Ulingan Bay, Papua New Guinea following the establishment of a self-sustaining timber surfboard factory within the local community. 

Nothing But Blue by @seabassb_ following German Olympic surfer Tim Elter

Princess by @mosmlbrn and surfer Harry Martin as they travel from The Great Australian Bite to Indonesia.

A note from this year’s Kickoff Ride leaders:

Hello Portland ✨️

We are a Dad and daughter duo (Perry & Jinx) who love riding and rolling with our lovely Portland peeps. Whether rollin on skates, or bikes we’ve had so many joyous, whimsical, educational, and heartfelt experiences over the last years rolling with you all through our streets, hanging in parks, store stops, and community spaces. 

You are our home, our community, our friends, and we’ve learned so much about our city, our neighbors, and ourselves.

We love that there is a something for everyone in our bike & skate friendly town and that our community is literally is what you make it. The way we look out for one another other and keep each other safe truly warms me up.

So it’s a real pleasure and we’re super excited to bring all of our youth riders of @kidicalmasspdx, and our amazing @bridge.city.skate together to help bring in this year’s Kickoff Ride.

No matter how you roll, we hope this is the beginning of a wonderful fun filled summer for all of you.

At 10.47am on the morning of 3 February 1931, the earth heaved upward and swayed violently.

A fault running directly beneath Napier and southwest across the Heretaunga Plains ruptured in a magnitude 7.8 earthquake.

Nearly all buildings in the central areas of Napier and Hastings were levelled, resulting in a devastating loss of life. Two hundred and fifty-six people across Hawke’s Bay were killed, making the 1931 Hawke’s Bay earthquake New Zealand’s deadliest natural disaster.

Thousands more were injured.

Today, we remember those lives lost, and we acknowledge the courage and determination of a community that rose from the rubble and ashes of that devastating event to imagine and create the very special city we call home today.

It is of great importance to @pj.wiley and Jinx, this year’s Kickoff Ride leaders, that the ride be welcoming and safer for skaters, kids, and other vulnerable road users. 

So, in addition to consulting with @josepheisenberg of @kidicalmasspdx to get tips on building a kid-friendly route, PJ invited two skaters, @kiki_kaska and @johnkoeger, to be a part of the planning committee.

Katie has been in the Portland skate community for 6 years with skate park, city skating and rink experience. She was introduced to the bike community through skate friendly rides and started biking in 2024. Katie enjoys designing, sewing and making clothing and items for themed events. 

Regarding her experience helping plan this year’s Kickoff Ride, she says, “Community members come together for the Kickoff Ride hopeful for summer fun to come. Being a part of the planning is a really special way to feel connected to that shared joy.”

John Koeger has been skating and biking in Portland for the past 4 years. His passion is growing the skate community in Portland and he enjoys music biking for any ride leaders looking for music. 

When PJ asked him to speak more on what excites them to be a part of Kickoff Ride planning, he said “While Shift calendar fun goes year round, for many people the Bike Summer Kickoff Ride is a call to dust off their bikes and get out riding and I’m excited to be a part of that energy.”

Want to support the ride this year? PJ is hosting a corker training and planning workshop TOMORROW (5/23) at 1pm. Meet at Grant High School on the 36th Ave side.

From Ecstatic Dance and live music to concerts and Kirtan, sound, vibration and frequency accompany us throughout the festival.

And because this is a Sober Festival, there’s no alcohol. Just music, movement, connection and that beautiful natural high that comes from dancing freely and being fully alive.

Different sounds. Different vibrations. One community.

Under Waters 🌀🐚🐚
FRIENDS WITH COMPUTERS: 
April Phillips, Jordan East, Pat Younis
19 February - 29 March @pica_perth @perthfest 
12-5 PM, Tues- Sun

11:13 mins (loop)
Complex Digital Object (moving image, sound, real-time body tracking, digital sculptures, photogrammetry scans, animation, particle systems), polyester tassels, cotton / polyester rugs, aluminium and polyvinyl.

2025 boorda yeyi Immersive Arts Commission Under Waters uncovers a speculative past of 500,000,000 (five hundred million) years ago when the majority of Earth’s surface was submerged in water. Streamed as a seamless loop, this moving image work operates as a portal—an all-access pass to a seemingly impossible dreaming— presenting ‘now’ in parallel to ‘long ago’ as a step to actualise deep time.

Extending the immense spatial and temporal scale of the work, Under Waters operates as a site for real-time play and interaction. The presence of the audience’s bodies mirror in the digital world, creating cause and effect in the unfolding scene. Immersed within the continuum of an ancient saltwater wonderland, audiences become inhabitants—activating this thriving world through movement and attentiveness.

The depths of the ocean floor present deep-water canyons, coral seas and rich kelp forests; an expansive and interconnected ecosystem. The slow propulsion through the deep reveals a rip, opening to a galactic sky: stars, nebula and infinite blackness—a reminder that deep oceans
and sky are connected as one; opposing points of truth that anchor the universe.

Under Waters is the inaugural recipient of PICA’s boorda yeyi Immersive Arts Commission. boorda yeyi, meaning ‘future now’ in Whadjuk Noongar language, is a program dedicated to expanding artistic practice through the use of technology, contributing to new ways of understanding, producing and experiencing contemporary art in Australia.

About Rambo:

Rambo Estrada is a surf adventure photographer based in New Zealand.

Although Mt Maunganui is his home, Rambo feels most alive when on the road. He spends the majority of his time on solo trips, living in his Land Rover seeking out the untouched remote coastlines of Aotearoa. Rambo is obsessed with finding isolated empty waves, aiming to infuse the raw beauty and tranquility of his homeland into every surf image he creates. Rambo also enjoys documenting the unique and often overlooked aspects of rural New Zealand life. Finding inspiration from the quirky offbeat charm you’ll only stumble across on the forgotten back roads.

Rambo is a self-taught photographer, but being a total math geek what originally attracted Rambo to photography was a fascination with the exposure triangle! He still digs the technical side of photography and gets a kick out of shooting every photo with the most efficient and economical settings aiming for each shot to be technically perfect. Rambo is very open with his photography knowledge and for him, the joy lies not only in capturing extraordinary moments but also in empowering others to embark on their own photographic journeys. 

Catch Rambo's submission to Flotsam's International Masters of Surf at the exhibition in May

Flotsam International Masters of Surf spotlight: @russellordphoto

International Masters of Surf is a carefully curated gathering of the world’s most influential surf photographers, whose work has helped shape surfing’s visual history. 

Photo: @russellordphoto 

About Russell:

Russell Ord is an Australian photographer best known for his striking surf and ocean photography.

Ord grew up playing Rugby League, Surfing and working as a firefighter. He began pursuing photography seriously in the early 2000s and quickly made a name for himself with his intense, dramatic images of big-wave surfing and ocean landscapes.

Ord’s work has been featured in numerous publications, including The Surfer’s Journal, Tracks, and Australian Surfing Life, and he has won multiple awards for his photography. He is particularly well known for his willingness to take risks in pursuit of the perfect shot, often putting himself in dangerous situations to capture the power and beauty of the ocean. Russ’s unique talents culminated in documenting a violent twist of the Indian Ocean known simply as ‘The Right’ in pursuit of a unique, career-defining angle. The hard-won image was the focal point for his celebrated documentary, ‘One Shot’.

He has worked with organizations such as the Surfrider Foundation and is an ambassador for SurfAid, helping to improve the health, well-being and resilience of remote communities connected to us through surfing. While he remains a passionate and astute chronicler of the ocean’s moods, Today, Russ, along with his wife Catherine, work towards providing education, mentoring and training in photography to young people who otherwise would be limited to having no access due to location, financial, social and health disadvantages through the Desert Light Foundation.

caption:
Unfocused dilettante, nay, Professional Artist DandyLion has been cycling around Portland for the past 11 years, after leaving their homeland in the Rocky Mountain foothills for a public service job in the City of Roses. Working in a mix of media ranging from experiential and wearable art to drag puppetry, they strive to ignite whimsy and fun. Their most infamous project is likely Sparklerocket, an illuminated discoball spaceship that launches every June for its annual Galactic Disco Pedalpalooza Voyage to the cosmic event @loudnlitride. When not making art, they are aspiring to live in a world in which billionaires are taxed out of existence and Palestine is free. 

Instagram: @dandyliondrag 
Email: DandyLionDrag@Gmail.com

—
DandyLion caught my eye first because of the joyous photos that attendees would post from their ride, and then last year I noticed their incredible poster. It always impresses me when organizers make a flier to promote their ride and this one was… out of this world!

Their ride listing had similar flair - “Costumes strongly advised (any combination of 70s garb, space or sci-fi themed clothing, robot attire, space creatures, sparkles, shinies, light-up stuff, etc). Medium pace. 6ish Miles. Not a loop. Dance breaks inevitable. BYO snacks and drinks. Cars are the mind-killer. The Disco must flow.”

So I reached out to see if Dandy would be willing to do this year’s Bike Summer poster art and merch, and to our collective joy - he said “Gasp! Yeah! I’d be honored”

Enjoy these photos of him hosting the inaugural Galactic Disco ride in 2017, leading the Galactic Disco in 2025, and DJing a halloween party, as well as the poster that won us over.

Link to the stellar merch he designed in our bio.

- Meghan

Projects like Skate of Mind show how grassroots sport and creativity can bridge cultures and strengthen lasting people-to-people connections between Australia and China.

Flotsam International Masters of Surf spotlight: @chrisburkard 

Chris Burkard is an accomplished explorer, photographer, creative director, speaker, and author.

Traveling throughout the year to pursue the farthest expanses of Earth, Burkard works to capture stories that inspire humans to consider their relationship with nature, while promoting the preservation of wild places everywhere.

Layered by outdoor, travel, adventure, surf, and lifestyle subjects, Burkard is known for images that are punctuated by untamed, powerful landscapes. Through social media, Chris strives to share his vision of wild places with millions of people, and to inspire them to explore for themselves.

His visionary perspective has earned him opportunities to work on global, prominent campaigns with Fortune 500 clients, speak on the TED stage, design product lines, educate, and publish a growing collection of books. Along with his team, Burkard is based out of his production studio and art gallery in the Central Coast of California.

At the age of 36, Burkard has established himself as a global presence and influence. He is happiest with his wife Breanne raising their two sons Jeremiah and Forrest in his hometown of Pismo Beach, California. 

Don’t miss Chris's submission to Flotsam’s International Masters of Surf, on display when the exhibition returns as part of the May festival.

Flotsam International Masters of Surf spotlight: Christa Funk @instaclamfunk

Photos by @instaclamfunk

About Christa:

In 2003, Christa was handed an SLR camera and was hooked after the initial shutter release. Her first assignment was to photograph an object of great personal significance. She chose a portrait of a Russian doll her parents had given her. During the development process, she made an error that ruined the entire roll of film except for one picture. She received an A for that image, and that was when she realized she had a knack for photography.

Fast forward nine years, Christa was a fresh Coast Guard Academy graduate assigned to Coast Guard Cutter RUSH in Hawaii. All her life she had been a competitive swimmer, and now she had the opportunity to learn how to surf. While learning, she became interested in surf photography, which combined her two passions—swimming and shooting.

After completing her time as a Coast Guard Officer, Christa transitioned into being a full-time photographer. In and out of the water, she pursues her passion by creating images that tell a story. She is fortunate to document places most people don’t get to see, while being surrounded by some of the best water people on earth. She is thrilled to share her adventures, hoping her photos will inspire others to explore the incredible world that God has created.

Please feel free to contact Christa regarding prints and projects using the contact form on the website. She currently resides on Oahu. 

Catch Christa’s submission to Flotsam’s International Masters of Surf when the exhibition returns during the May festival.

Flotsam International Masters of Surf spotlight: @browncannoniii

International Masters of Surf brings together a hand-selected group of the world’s foremost surf photographers, honouring their lasting impact on the visual history of surfing. 

Photo: @browncannoniii

About Brown:

Brown began his photographic journey in his parents’ darkroom over 40 years ago. He studied at the Art Center College of Design in Pasadena California and hit the ground running in the Fall of1999.

Brown has traveled to more than 50 countries photographing award winning stories for editorial and commercial clients including Travel & Leisure, Conde Nast, National Geographic Adventure, Outside, GEO Saison and Copalli Rum. Passionate for culture, adventure and conservation, Brown has camped in the Empty Quarter and been diving with Great White Sharks in Guadalupe, Mexico. He has ridden 120 miles on horseback through the Mongolian Steppe with the Altai Mountain Eagle Hunters and has sailed through the Arctic Glaciers of Svalbard. But when asked, “Where is the one place on Earth that resonates more with him than any other?” He answers unequivocally, “the Seven Mile Miracle known as the North Shore of Oahu.”

Cannon’s photography has been exhibited in solo and group gallery shows in galleries and museums in California, Oregon, Colorado, New Mexico, South Carolina, New York and Hawaii, and is in numerous private collections. In 2009 Brown Co-Founded Intersection Photos, a boutique travel stock photography company. In 2018 he founded no2plastic.org, a nonprofit dedicated to reducing single-use plastics for the benefit of human and planet health. His new book NORTH is a portrait of the North Shore of Oahu and was released by Damiani October 2023. Brown divides his time between Oregon and Hawaii.

International Masters of Surf is an exclusive assembly of the world’s most influential surf photographers, whose imagery has defined the visual legacy of surfing 

About Cait:

Cait Miers is a surf photographer originally from the Mornington Peninsula, Victoria, and currently based in Byron Bay, NSW.

Having completed a Bachelor of Photography at Melbourne’s RMIT University in 2014, her unique and authentic approach to photography has seen her working with clients from all over the world. She’s one of the leading women’s surf photographers in the industry, and that was her dream right from the start. Her goal is to inspire elegance and femininity in women’s surfing, and continue to shoot people and places from all walks of life!

Cait’s fashion based work has grown rapidly over the past few years, and she is passionate about conceptualising her clients vision and bringing it to life, with her own twist of course. Recently working with high profile clients such as WSL, Roxy, Billabong, Cotton On, Teva, Contiki, Canon, FCS and Lululemon, as well as travel tourism bodies in the Northern Territory, WA and Victoria, Cait is dedicated to following her passion covering a diverse range of stories through her photography.

“I want to inspire women. That’s my main goal. To be brave, to chase their dreams, to live life to the full. It’s not just about photography, but the stories behind the image, the tougher moments, the travel, the lifestyle. I want my images to make you feel something, anything.”

With a healthy following on Instagram, she’s continuing to expand her client base, traveling and shooting passion projects that don’t stem too far away from the water!

See Cait’s submission to Flotsam’s International Masters of Surf when the exhibition returns this May

What an unforgettable afternoon at Adore Chef’s Table with Gareth Whitton from Tarts Anon during Ubud Food Festival 2026.

More than 60 pastry chefs, bakers, chocolatiers, and F&B professionals gathered to experience something truly special: three beautiful Tarts Anon-style tarts crafted using Adore Cacao, alongside the official launch of our Bali Single Origin chocolate.

Chef Gareth showcased his creativity by incorporating beautiful Indonesian ingredients into each tart, creating flavors that felt both familiar and exciting. Every bite told a story of craftsmanship, terroir, and thoughtful ingredient selection, making it a truly memorable experience for everyone in the room.

But this event was about more than just delicious desserts.

Throughout the tasting, we also shared something that sits at the heart of Adore: the importance of sustaining Indonesia’s cacao and vanilla farms.

At Adore, our mission goes beyond delivering premium quality chocolate and vanilla. We believe great ingredients begin with healthy farms, empowered farmers, and respect for the environment. Every product we make carries the hard work of many hands behind the scenes: from farm to chef’s table.

We know meaningful impact doesn’t happen overnight, but we believe in taking small steps, consistently.

Because in the end, true quality is not only about flavor, it is also about people, purpose, and sustainability.

About Damea:

Damea Dorsey stands as a luminary in the world of surf photography, a celebrated artist whose lens captures the heart and soul of oceanic adventures.

Originally from California and now calling Bali home, Damea’s photographic journey has taken him across the globe, from the legendary Pipeline to the towering waves of maxing Mexican beachbreaks.

His skill in shooting water imagery in the ocean’s most challenging lineups has earned him widespread acclaim, leading to collaborations with surfing’s most notable luminaries. As a Senior Staff Photographer for Transworld Surf, Damea’s work adorned the covers of esteemed publications such as Transworld Surf, Australian Surfing Life, Stab, Waves, Surf Europe, ZigZag, and more.

Damea’s talent extends beyond editorial work, as he has secured corporate partnerships with top-tier brands including Red Bull, Hurley, Volcom, Billabong, and Quiksilver. His photographs not only capture the raw power and beauty of the ocean but also evoke a sense of adventure and freedom that resonates with audiences worldwide.

With an unparalleled eye for detail and a relentless pursuit of perfection, Damea Dorsey continues to push the boundaries of surf photography. His images serve as a testament to the enduring allure of the sea and the indomitable spirit of those who ride its waves.

Surf Buddies.

Hard to miss and impossible to forget.

If you’ve spent enough time around a Surfing NSW event, you probably know Fluro Phil.

You might not know his real name.

For more than 15 years, Phil Mansfield has kept NSW events running as a beach marshal, measuring boards, handing out event packs, making sure things run smoothly. 

Wondering where the nickname came from? Don’t look further than his outfits.

Long before the matching hats and event gear, Phil was the guy riding a nine foot longboard in the brightest fluorescent colour he could find.

The name stuck. 

It’s followed him ever since. At this year’s State Classic, the site crew turned up in matching orange fluro raincoats when the rain came in. Phil took one look, disappeared, and came back in yellow. Somehow still the brightest person on site.

Fluro has been a part of NSW longboarding for decades. Long enough to remember running BBQs just to scrape together judging fees, and long enough to watch that turn into fully computerised scoring. 

He might live north of Brisbane these days, but there’s one thing that hasn’t changed.

Phil’s loyalty to NSW.

“I’d love to enter competition again, but couldn’t on behalf of Qld because I’m a diehard NSW man.”

He’s NSW through and through.

And one of the familiar faces that makes NSW surfing what it is.

#SurfingNSW

Flotsam International Masters of Surf spotlight: @billmorris

International Masters of Surf is a handpicked roll call of the world’s foremost lens folk that showcases their contribution to the history of surf photography. 
Photo: @billmorris

About Bill: 

Bill grew up in Bondi, Sydney. He learned to surf at a very young age, his father pushing him into small waves at North Bondi.

Bill was always interested in photography and bought a professional camera and lens as soon as he could save enough money.

Bill loved to shoot slide film and would have his friends around to his house for slide nights, loading up the projector with his early surf adventures in Indonesia and display them
big on the wall for them all to see. It was fortunate for Bill that a prominent @tracksmag photographer, Tony Nolan, attended one of his slide shows and offered to take a few of Bill’s images into the Tracks office to show the editor. And so began the career Bill never quite saw coming.

As Bill began to get published, he bought a water housing for his camera and began shooting from the water. After winning an Australian Surfing Photography Award for Best Water
Shot in 1998, he was signed as a Senior Photographer by US Surfing Magazine and also Australia’s Surfing Life in Queensland and began travelling the globe on assignments with the world’s best surfers. Companies, which included Oakley and O’Neill, also began hiring Bill to shoot their surfers for advertising campaigns.

Today, Bill mainly concentrates on his Ocean Landscape business. Selling acrylics and framed prints of Sydney’s coastline via his website. However, he still has a close
relationship with Tracks Magazine and Surfline, who he mainly submits his surfing imagery to these days

Catch Bill's submission to Flotsam's International Masters of Surf at the exhibition when it return during the festival in May

This saturday, Isabel Costa presents the show 𝑴𝒂𝒏𝒊𝒇𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒐𝒔 𝒇𝒐𝒓 𝑨𝒇𝒕𝒆𝒓 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝑬𝒏𝒅 𝒐𝒇 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝑾𝒐𝒓𝒍𝒅, a production with Os Possessos, co-produced by Walk&Talk Biennial.

Inspired by the curatorial work of Hans Ulrich Obrist, seven actors give voice to manifestos written after the year 2000, guiding the audience through different spaces of the Palácio da Conceição (one of the headquarters of the Azores Government). 

Each text is shared in close proximity with a small group of spectators, subverting the traditional, declamatory style of manifesto readings. At its core lies the desire to speak attentively to the urgencies of today — delivering words of hope and denunciation, reflections on the world, and fragments of everyday life.

💬 Sessions are in Portuguese and take place every 30 minutes.

|

Neste sábado, Isabel Costa apresenta o espetáculo 𝑴𝒂𝒏𝒊𝒇𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒐𝒔 𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂 𝑫𝒆𝒑𝒐𝒊𝒔 𝒅𝒐 𝑭𝒊𝒎 𝒅𝒐 𝑴𝒖𝒏𝒅𝒐, uma produção Os Possessos co-produzida pela Bienal Walk&Talk. 

Inspirados pelo trabalho curatorial de Hans Ulrich Obrist, sete atores dão voz a manifestos recentes (escritos após o ano 2000), conduzindo o público por diferentes espaços do Palácio da Conceição (uma das sedes do Governo dos Açores). 

Cada texto é partilhado em proximidade com um pequeno grupo de espectadores, subvertendo o estilo tradicional e declamatório das leituras de manifestos. No seu centro está o desejo de falar atentamente às urgências do presente — entregando palavras de esperança e denúncia, reflexões sobre o mundo e fragmentos da vida quotidiana. 

💬 As sessões são em língua portuguesa e acontecem a cada 30 minutos.

It’s been a journey full of beautiful encounters — and we’re truly happy with the echoes this edition is already generating.

In this Biennial, as in life, acting from a place of abundance means working in a network: bringing people together, exchanging ways of doing, and opening space to imagine collectively. 

Thank you to all the artists, teams, facilitators, partners, sponsors and audiences for being part of this network. Your contribution made the first edition of Walk&Talk Biennial possible, allowing it to speak from the Azores to the Atlantic and beyond.

We’ll be sharing more in the coming months about 𝐺𝐸𝑆𝑇𝑈𝑅𝐸𝑆 𝑂𝐹 𝐴𝐵𝑈𝑁𝐷𝐴𝑁𝐶𝐸, as well as updates and news about our journey towards 2027. See you soon.

|

Foi um caminho repleto de encontros bonitos e estamos muito felizes com os ecos que esta edição está já a gerar. 

Nesta Bienal, como na vida, agir a partir da abundância é trabalhar em rede: aproximar pessoas, cruzar modos de fazer e abrir espaço para imaginar em conjunto. 

Obrigado a todas as equipas, artistas, pessoas mediadoras, parcerias, patrocinadores e públicos por fazerem parte desta rede. O vosso contributo tornou possível a primeira edição da Bienal Walk&Talk, permitindo que falasse a partir dos Açores para o Atlântico e além.

Nos próximos meses vamos partilhar mais sobre 𝐺𝐸𝑆𝑇𝑂𝑆 𝐷𝐸 𝐴𝐵𝑈𝑁𝐷𝐴̂𝑁𝐶𝐼𝐴 e também novidades sobre o caminho que agora iniciamos rumo a 2027. Até já.

—

Liquid Lens: introducing Ted Grambeau, one of the world’s most accomplished and well-travelled surf and adventure photographers. 

Drum roll... Fresh new episode from Flotsam's Liquid Lens interview series just dropped on the Flotsam Youtube channel, with this installment featuring Ted Grambeau.
.
Ted studied photography at RMIT university in Melbourne, and worked as an assistant to legendary photographer Burt Glinn, of Magnum photo agency, in New York, giving his work a solid technical foundation. Ted is highly experienced in advertising, corporate and editorial work with an accent on shooting in, on, around, and under water. His focus is on lifestyle, portraiture, fashion swimwear, action sports and surf adventure; specialising in extreme locations with a focus on problem solving and providing solutions for clients. “My passion is to create visually powerful and emotionally evocative imagery.” 
.
What is Liquid Lens? The Gold Coast’s legendary strip of surf breaks has long been a creative playground for global surf brands and competitive athletes. Liquid Lens dives deeper than just the pixel-perfect lineup shots, showcasing the ocean-based filmmakers and photographers who capture the waves and their riders, while illuminating their artistry, inspirations, and passion for the sea. Em Manifestos Para Depois do Fim do Mundo sete atores interpretam diferentes manifestos, escritos depois de 2000. O espetáculo é apresentado ao público num percurso que passa por diversos espaços dentro e fora do Palácio da Conceição. Cada manifesto é dito de forma intimista, apenas para um pequeno grupo de espectadores, de forma a contrariar a leitura tradicional de um manifesto, que tende a ser panfletária. Está na base deste espetáculo a vontade de transmitir palavras atentas que nos falam do mundo de hoje. 

Depois de Dresden (Alemanha), Havana (Cuba), Ravenna (Itália), Manifestos Para Depois do Fim do Mundo é apresentado no Walk&Talk, co-produtor do espectáculo desde 2023. What an incredible day of skateboarding, connection, and community at our Adaptive Skate Jam in Culver City!

At THE SKATESIDE, we believe skateboarding is so much more than learning tricks or riding a board. It’s about building confidence, discovering what’s possible, overcoming challenges, and finding a community where everyone belongs.

This event was a reminder of just how powerful skateboarding can be when we create opportunities for people of all abilities to participate, learn, and express themselves.

Throughout the day, we witnessed determination, courage, encouragement, and plenty of smiles. From trying something new to celebrating personal accomplishments, every moment reminded us why we do what we do.

💙 Different abilities. Different journeys. One skateboarding community.

In celebration of National Disability Employment Awareness Month, we wanted to bring people together and create an environment where adaptive skaters could feel welcomed, supported, and empowered.

Because skateboarding isn’t about being the best person at the skatepark. It’s about challenging yourself, progressing at your own pace, supporting others, and enjoying the ride.

A huge THANK YOU to every participant, family, volunteer, coach, and community member who came out and made this event special. Your energy, encouragement, and enthusiasm are what make events like this possible.

We’re especially grateful to everyone who continues to support our mission of creating more inclusive opportunities through skateboarding.

Our hope is that events like this inspire more families, communities, and organizations to recognize that skateboarding has a place for EVERYONE.

And we’re just getting started! 🚀

🍍 𝑺𝑴𝑶𝑶𝑻𝑯 𝑪𝑨𝒀𝑬𝑵𝑵𝑬 𝑵𝑶𝑻𝑬𝑺 @maelokko

𝑺𝒎𝒐𝒐𝒕𝒉 𝑪𝒂𝒚𝒆𝒏𝒏𝒆 𝑵𝒐𝒕𝒆𝒔 is a natural-dye textile installation that traces the global journeys of the pineapple since the 19th century, exploring its ecology and hidden bonds with other plants through color. While the fruit’s form and sweetness have long captivated imaginations, its potential as a source of dyes from roots, leaves, and rinds has been less examined. Plant-based color, historically tied to systems of value, also acts as an archive of soil health, biodiversity, and environmental memory.

The work brings together around one hundred textile squares, dyed with plants and soils from the Americas, Europe, Africa, and the Pacific. Using dye-baths from pineapple rinds and leaves on piña fiber, the installation generates a “plantone” catalogue mapping the plant’s entanglements with other species and territories. 

📍Boa Fruta – Plantação de Ananases, Rua das Laranjeiras, Ponta Delgada
👀 Can be visited until 𝟑𝟎.𝟏𝟏

|

𝑺𝒎𝒐𝒐𝒕𝒉 𝑪𝒂𝒚𝒆𝒏𝒏𝒆 𝑵𝒐𝒕𝒆𝒔 é uma instalação têxtil com tingimentos naturais que traça as viagens globais do ananás desde o século XIX, explorando a sua ecologia e as ligações ocultas com outras plantas através da cor. Enquanto a forma e a doçura do fruto há muito cativam o imaginário, o seu potencial como fonte de corantes obtidos a partir de raízes, folhas e cascas têm sido menos explorado. A cor de origem vegetal, historicamente associada a sistemas de valor, funciona também como arquivo da saúde do solo, da biodiversidade e da memória ambiental.

A obra reúne cerca de uma centena de quadrados têxteis, tingidos com plantas e solos das Américas, Europa, África e Pacífico. Utilizando banhos de tingimento feitos a partir de cascas e folhas de ananás sobre fibra de piña, a instalação gera um catálogo de “plantones” que mapeia os entrelaçamentos da planta com outras espécies e territórios. 

—

“I can’t believe the coach let him do that!”

That might be your first thought watching this video.

What you don’t see is everything that happened before this moment.

This was his very first time on a skateboard.

Before he ever stood at the top of this ramp, he learned the fundamentals. He practiced balance, proper stance, how to fall safely, speed control, and how to stay relaxed on the board. Our coach evaluated him every step of the way and only introduced the next challenge when he was ready.

By the time he reached the top, this wasn’t a gamble.

It was the next step in his progression.

At THE SKATESIDE, we don’t rush kids into obstacles they’re not prepared for. We believe confidence is earned through patience, encouragement, repetition, and great coaching.

The best part wasn’t that he made it down the ramp.

It was the look on his face afterward. He realized he was capable of something he never imagined doing just an hour earlier. Moments like these build confidence that extends far beyond skateboarding.

If you’ve been thinking about getting your child into skateboarding, our Summer Camps are the perfect place to start.

Curiosity guided the process, allowing each one to find their own rhythm and their own way of looking.

Between sharing, small experiments, and informal conversations, cinema became less technical and more of a meeting point: a way of being and imagining together and revealing the beauty that emerges when we allow ourselves to observe with time.

Through conversations, attempts, and discoveries, they practice 𝐺𝐸𝑆𝑇𝑈𝑅𝐸𝑆 𝑂𝐹 𝐴𝐵𝑈𝑁𝐷𝐴𝑁𝐶𝐸 and test new ways of looking at the island that welcomes us.

Curated by Rita Serra e Silva and Rita Westwood, and a dedicated mediation team — Cristóvão Maçarico, Dryelle Andrade, Luís Senra, Samantha Ruggiero, and Sofia Botelho (in partnership with Arquipélago – Centro de Artes Contemporâneas) — the 𝐁𝐞𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐭 axis of 𝐒𝐈𝐍𝐓𝐎𝐍𝐈𝐙𝐀𝐑 – 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐬 𝐏𝐮́𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐨𝐬 will continue until the end of the Biennial.

|

As 𝐕𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐬 𝐎𝐟𝐢𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐚𝐬 do programa 𝐒𝐈𝐍𝐓𝐎𝐍𝐈𝐙𝐀𝐑 têm vindo a transformar cada 𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑐̧𝑎̃𝑜 da Bienal num ponto de encontro vivo entre pessoas, ideias e modos de fazer. 

Adaptadas às especificidades de cada escola, instituição ou comunidade participante, estas visitas-oficina são desenhadas como pequenos laboratórios de experimentação: seguros, acessíveis, inclusivos e sempre abertos ao inesperado. Entre conversas, tentativas e descobertas, praticam-se 𝐺𝐸𝑆𝑇𝑂𝑆 𝐷𝐸 𝐴𝐵𝑈𝑁𝐷𝐴̂𝑁𝐶𝐼𝐴 e testam-se novas formas de olhar para a ilha que nos acolhe.

Com curadoria de Rita Serra e Silva e Rita Westwood, e uma equipa de mediação dedicada — Cristóvão Maçarico, Dryelle Andrade, Luís Senra, Samantha Ruggiero e Sofia Botelho (em parceria com o Arquipélago – Centro de Artes Contemporâneas) — o eixo 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐫 do 𝐒𝐈𝐍𝐓𝐎𝐍𝐈𝐙𝐀𝐑 – 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐚𝐬 𝐏𝐮́𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐨𝐬 segue em andamento até ao final da Bienal.

Three artists from the Azorean diaspora are united by the concept of being “Saltborn”: those who, despite not living on the islands, remain rooted in their affective geography. Their works span sound, design, and visual art: folklore emerges as a living practice of community and memory; tourism is reframed as a new identity marker through visual codes legible mainly to Azoreans; and the diasporic experience in North America is evoked through reflections on absence and longing for a phantom home.

📍Rua Adolfo Coutinho, Ribeira Grande
👀 Open until 𝟑𝟎.𝟏𝟏 | Monday to Sunday, 10H–18H.

|

A exposição reúne três artistas da diáspora açoriana unidos pelo conceito de “Saltborn”: aqueles que, apesar de não viverem nas ilhas, permanecem enraizados na sua geografia afetiva. Os seus trabalhos atravessam som, design e artes visuais: o folclore surge como prática viva de comunidade e memória; o turismo é reformulado como um novo marcador de identidade através de códigos visuais legíveis sobretudo para açorianos; e a experiência diaspórica na América do Norte é evocada em reflexões sobre ausência e desejo de uma casa fantasma.

One of the most rewarding parts of what we do is showing young people that their passions can grow into something much bigger than they ever imagined.

Today I had the opportunity to visit @now_academy for Career Day and read our children’s book, @gromlinuniverse , to an amazing group of students. We talked about friendship, courage, perseverance, and the journey that led from being a kid who loved skateboarding to helping build @the_skateside and serving thousands of families throughout Southern California.

Career Day is about more than discussing jobs. It’s about helping students see possibilities. Whether their dream is to become an artist, athlete, teacher, entrepreneur, author, or something that hasn’t even been invented yet, every big journey starts with believing in yourself and taking that first step.

Thank you to the students, teachers, and staff at NOW Academy for welcoming us into your classroom. Seeing the excitement, curiosity, and imagination of these students reminds us why we do what we do.

At THE SKATESIDE, our mission has always been about more than skateboarding. We believe in building confidence, character, resilience, and creating positive experiences that help young people grow both on and off the board.

If you would like THE SKATESIDE to visit your school for a Career Day presentation, Meet the Author event, book reading, or student assembly, we’d love to connect. Reach out to learn more about bringing a Gromlin Universe author visit to your campus.

🙋 On 𝟒-𝟓.𝟏𝟏, Casa da Bienal hosted the 𝒉𝑨𝑵𝑫𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒈 workshop, and on 𝟖.𝟏𝟏, 𝑬𝒔𝒄𝒐𝒍𝒂 𝒅𝒐 𝑹𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒓, both promoted by AND Lab.

𝒉𝑨𝑵𝑫𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒈 introduced formal and non-formal educators to the philosophy of the 𝐴𝑁𝐷 𝑂𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑒 𝑀𝑜𝑑𝑒, created by Fernanda Eugénio. Through a game using objects with no apparent value, participants explored practices of reciprocity, attention, and coexistence, reflecting on care, listening, and the role of education in social transformation.

𝑬𝒔𝒄𝒐𝒍𝒂 𝒅𝒐 𝑹𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒓, open to the general public, invited everyone to play and reflect on how we relate to others and the world while practicing “not-knowing” together.
Two encounters that combined reflection, learning, unlearning, and the (trans)formative dimension of play and collective care.

|

Nos dias 𝟒-𝟓.𝟏𝟏, a Casa da Bienal recebeu o workshop 𝒉𝑨𝑵𝑫𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒈 e, no dia 𝟖.𝟏𝟏, a 𝑬𝒔𝒄𝒐𝒍𝒂 𝒅𝒐 𝑹𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒓, ambos promovidos pelo AND Lab.

O 𝒉𝑨𝑵𝑫𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒈 introduziu educadoras/es formais e não formais à filosofia do 𝑀𝑜𝑑𝑜 𝑂𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑜 𝐴𝑁𝐷, criado por Fernanda Eugénio. Através de um jogo com objetos sem valor aparente, os participantes exploraram práticas de reciprocidade, atenção e convivência, refletindo sobre o cuidado, a escuta e o papel da educação na transformação social.

Já a 𝑬𝒔𝒄𝒐𝒍𝒂 𝒅𝒐 𝑹𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒓 aberta ao público em geral, convidou todos a jogar e refletir sobre a forma como nos relacionamos com os outros e com o mundo, enquanto praticamos juntos o “não-saber”.

Dois encontros que combinaram reflexão, aprendizagem, desaprendizagem e a dimensão (trans)formativa do brincar e do cuidado coletivo.

—
📸 @marianalidl

Discover what goes into one of North Sumatra’s most beloved dishes, straight from the chef himself. Gerry Nainggolan reimagines the traditional Batak classic with Fish Tombur, featuring crispy fried fish topped with sambal tombur, a rich and fiery Batak relish built around the distinctive citrusy heat of andaliman pepper. 

A fresh kecombrang salsa brings fragrant, zesty crunch that cuts beautifully through the savoury depth and nutty spice of the fish, lifting the whole dish into something bright and alive. Bold, layered, and rooted in tradition, this is your chance to see North Sumatran cooking at its most confident.

Session supported by Cascades at Viceroy Bali.

LINK IN BIO (só disponível este fim de semana).

Mantendo-se fiel às edições anteriores, o Portuguese Surf Film Festival (PSFF), realizado na Ericeira, apresenta desde 2017 uma categoria dedicada — “Women in Surf Films” — que destaca histórias centradas nas mulheres e no mar. Ao longo dos anos, o festival tem exibido filmes que revelam a diversidade das experiências femininas no surf, celebrando tanto surfistas como cineastas num setor tradicionalmente dominado por homens, e abordando temas como resiliência, paixão pelo desporto e consciência ambiental.

Nesta homenagem ao dia 8 de março, o festival apresenta seis filmes disponíveis na sua landing page em portuguesesurffilmfestival.com. Alguns deles já fizeram parte de edições anteriores do PSFF, que em 2026 celebra 15 anos de história.

What remains when repair is no longer possible? The future might be a tedious place, and yet, within this tedium, 𝑩𝑨𝑵𝑫𝑶 imagines abundance as a hall of mirrors — levitating over commonplaces, moving without brakes, fragile and unstoppable.

𝑩𝑨𝑵𝑫𝑶 is a new commission by 37.25 - Núcleo de Artes Performativas, a collective founded by dancers from São Miguel that has become a key platform for contemporary dance in the Azores. Rooted in the island’s heritage and geography, their work develops through interdisciplinarity and collaborations across artistic fields. For this project, they invited choreographer Daniela Cruz to create a piece in dialogue with the group.

More info at walktalkazores.org
Tickets via teatromicaelense.pt

O que resta quando já não é possível reparar? O futuro pode parecer um lugar enfadonho, e  ainda assim, dentro desse tédio, 𝑩𝑨𝑵𝑫𝑶 imagina a abundância como uma sala de espelhos — a levitar sobre lugares-comuns, a mover-se sem travões, frágil e imparável.

🌿 On saturday morning, Cooking Sections shared with us some of their long-term research and work examining food systems and the imprints of extractivism in places like Istanbul and Puglia, before Raquel Vargas shared her experience with BioKairós in organic production on the island. Apolo de Carvalho, Sónia Vaz Borges and César Schofield Cardoso traced some of the histories of Cape Verdean resistance, collective memory and belonging through diasporic movement.

In the afternoon at vaga, Candice Lin reflected on how the aesthetic and temporal qualities of stones unsettle human notions of life and non-life, showing us her artistic experimentation using minerals, metals and other natural materials. In a workshop, Mirna Bamieh took us on a sensory journey into sourness, to explore active listening through the transformative lens of fermentation, weaving together themes of care, self-awareness and connection to place.

|

No sábado de manhã, os Cooking Sections partilharam o seu trabalho e investigação de longo termo sobre sistemas alimentares e as marcas do extrativismo em lugares como Istambul e Puglia, seguidos da partilha de Raquel Vargas sobre a sua experiência com a BioKairós em produção biológica na ilha. Apolo de Carvalho, Sónia Vaz Borges e César Schofield Cardoso traçaram algumas das histórias da resistência cabo-verdiana, da sua memória coletiva e sentimentos de pertença através de movimentos diaspóricos.

À tarde, na vaga, Candice Lin refletiu sobre como as qualidades estéticas e temporais das pedras perturbam noções humanas de vida e não-vida, partilhando a sua prática artística com minerais, metais e outros elementos naturais. No seu workshop, Mirna Bamieh levou-nos numa viagem sensorial pela acidez, explorando a escuta ativa através da lente transformadora da fermentação, tecendo temas como o cuidado, a autoconsciência e a ligação ao lugar.

—
📸 @marianalidl
