At the Convent — once a place of enclosure and discipline — a field now opens to experiment with these non-normative modes of knowledge. Here, abundance is measured not by accumulation but by bonds: what moves between species, what is preserved and transformed with time, what resists domestication, what lingers in detail and memory.

Such practices remind us that to learn and to teach is not only to reproduce institutional gestures, but to take part in collective, ecological, and imaginative movements. This station invites us to tune into knowledges that flow along the edges and to recognise in them the possibility of rehearsing other ways of living in common.

📍Rua de Santo António, Santa Cruz, Lagoa
👀 Open until 𝟐𝟖.𝟏𝟏 | Monday to Friday, 9H30–13H / 14H–17H30.

|

No Convento — outrora lugar de clausura e disciplina — abre-se agora um campo para experimentar estes modos não normativos de conhecimento. Aqui, a abundância mede-se não pela acumulação, mas pelos vínculos: o que circula entre espécies, o que se conserva e transforma com o tempo, o que resiste à domesticação, o que perdura no detalhe e na memória. 

Estas práticas lembram-nos que aprender e ensinar não é apenas reproduzir gestos institucionais, mas participar em movimentos coletivos, ecológicos e imaginativos. Esta estação convida-nos a sintonizar saberes que fluem pelas margens e a reconhecer neles a possibilidade de ensaiar outras formas de viver em comum.

It is a rumination on breathing in circumstances that should be impossible. É uma meditação sobre o respirar em circunstâncias que deveriam ser impossíveis. Vivemos numa ordem global que se alimenta da violência que impede — humanos, não humanos, seres vivos em geral — de respirar. Uma ordem em que os sonhos de uns simplesmente devoram os dos outros.

Soundsplash takes place on a beautiful reserve overlooking Ngarunui Beach in Whāingaroa, Raglan. This place is more than just a spot for a festival - it’s a shared community space, cared for by locals and mana whenua who generously welcome us each year.

We’re committed to minimising our impact, but it’s up to all of us to protect this special place. If we work together we can maximise our efforts.

Here’s how you can help:
1️⃣ Take everything home with you. ESPECIALLY your tent.
2️⃣ Use the recycling bins provided.
3️⃣ Invest in decent camping gear instead of cheap stuff that won’t last.
4️⃣ Avoid single-use plastics. Reusable is the way to go.
5️⃣ Bin your rubbish & don’t leave it lying around.
6️⃣ Leave no trace - keep your campsite as you found it.
7️⃣ Remind your mates to do the same.

Let’s make it one to remember. 🌿 No trace. No tent left behind

𝑫𝑬𝑺𝑪𝑶𝑳𝑨’s exhibition now moves to the second municipality where it will be presented on the island.

Over a period of six months, six young people from São Miguel were encouraged to travel and think creatively about the importance of living under a logic of abundance. Their creations will tour the six municipalities of São Miguel between 2025 and 2026, organized by curators and museographers Diogo Sousa and José Amorim, after their inauguration in September at @parque.atlantico.

👀 The exhibition can be visited until the end of the Biennial!

|

A exposição do 𝑫𝑬𝑺𝑪𝑶𝑳𝑨 parte agora para o Museu Municipal da Ribeira Grande, segundo município da ilha em que irá ser apresentada.

Ao longo de seis meses, seis jovens de São Miguel foram provocados a deslocar-se e descolar criativamente para refletir sobre a importância de vivermos sob lógicas de abundância. As suas criações são apresentadas no âmbito da Bienal Walk&Talk, e percorrem os seis municípios de São Miguel entre 2025 e 2026, organizadas pela curadoria e museografia de Diogo Sousa e José Amorim, após a sua inauguração em setembro no @parque.atlantico.

📍 Ponto de encontro / Meeting point: Teatro Ribeiragrandense, Ribeira Grande

Guarda Rios (or River Guards) make their debut researching São Miguel’s river basins and, through their River Observatory, engage students from Ribeira Grande High School to create playful devices that foster ecological knowledge and collective creation — because nothing awakens shared memory more than a splash of water. During the Symposium, the collective shares the experiences of this workshop with participants in collaboration with Paula Aguiar, bringing the symposium outdoors and into the flow of the rivers.

🚌 Free shuttle available at 14H30 to Ribeira Grande and back to Ponta Delgada at 17H30.

⛅ If the weather allows, this event takes place outdoors. It is recommended to bring a raincoat, comfortable clothes and shoes. 

–

O Coletivo Guarda Rios estreia-se a investigar as bacias hidrográficas de São Miguel e, através do seu Observatório das Ribeiras, envolve estudantes da Ribeira Grande na criação de dispositivos lúdicos que estimulam o conhecimento ecológico e a criação coletiva — porque nada desperta melhor a memória partilhada do que um mergulho na água. Durante o Simpósio, o coletivo partilha as experiências desta oficina com o público, em colaboração com Paula Aguiar, levando o simpósio para fora de portas e para o fluxo dos rios.

🚌 Transfer gratuito disponível às 14H30 para a Ribeira Grande e de volta a Ponta Delgada às 17H30.

@cata.couto.g · @cesarfilipa · @megstuart33 · @monicademiranda_studio · @resolvecollective

What forms of knowledge remain at the margins of established circuits? How are they transmitted when they do not fit within the school, the textbook, or the archive? This station invites us to think of pedagogy as an aesthetic and political practice, where learning and teaching merge with gestures of resistance, fabulation, and collective imagination.

At vaga, the Biennial opens a field of listening and transmission that challenges disciplinary boundaries and reactivates insurgent pedagogies. Learning emerges as an act of imagination, attention, and dissidence.

📍Travessa das Laranjeiras, 51, Ponta Delgada
👀 Open until 𝟐𝟗.𝟏𝟏 | Thursday to Saturday, 14H–18H

🧵The materials for this exhibition were generously borrowed by MBrum, Herdeiros de Agostinho Medeiros and Lotaçor.

|

Que formas de conhecimento permanecem à margem dos circuitos instituídos? Como se transmitem quando não cabem na escola, no manual ou no arquivo? Esta estação convida-nos a pensar a pedagogia como prática estética e política, onde aprender e ensinar se confundem com gestos de resistência, fabulação e imaginação coletiva.

Na vaga, a Bienal abre um campo de escuta e transmissão que desafia fronteiras disciplinares e reativa pedagogias insurgentes. Aprender surge como ato de imaginação, de atenção e de dissidência.

—

In this station, the body appears as a suspended territory — a surface where habits, gestures, and ways of being are inscribed, but also a place of projection, silence, and listening. 

Through photography and sculpture, the works presented here outline a relational cartography: images and forms that interlace, suggesting connections between bodies, infrastructures, and landscapes of the Azores and other Atlantic archipelagos. They are fragments of the same inquiry into presence and impermanence, into how we inscribe ourselves in territories of water, stone, and light.

📍Rua Dr. Guilherme Poças Falcão, 23, Ponta Delgada
👀 Open until 𝟐𝟗.𝟏𝟏 | Monday to Saturday, 10H–19H.

Nesta estação, o corpo surge como um território suspenso — uma superfície onde se inscrevem hábitos, gestos e modos de estar, mas também um lugar de projeção, silêncio e escuta. 

Através da fotografia e da escultura, as obras aqui apresentadas delineiam uma cartografia relacional: imagens e formas que se entrelaçam, sugerindo conexões entre corpos, infraestruturas e paisagens dos Açores e de outros arquipélagos atlânticos. São fragmentos da mesma investigação sobre presença e impermanência, sobre como nos inscrevemos em territórios de água, pedra e luz.

The 𝒉𝑨𝑵𝑫𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒈 workshop introduces participants to the philosophy of the AND Operating Mode, created by Fernanda Eugénio. It consists of presenting and practicing a game that rethinks reciprocity and attention, opening space for living together in a (trans)formative and shared dimension.

Aimed at education professionals from all levels and areas of teaching, the workshop invites collective reflection on what a school committed to care, listening, and social transformation might look like.

As part of 𝐒𝐈𝐍𝐓𝐎𝐍𝐈𝐙𝐀𝐑 – 𝐏𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐬.

Consiste na apresentação e no exercício de um jogo que repensa práticas de reciprocidade, atenção e do viver junto, permitindo uma dimensão (trans)formativa e de partilha.

The Skate of Mind crew rolled up to Wentworth St on Saturday 18th April, took over a vacant lot, and turned it into a skate session for the whole community. Our pro team threw down some demos and helped first-timers find the courage to drop in on the ramp — those moments never get old. 🤙
1 street. 10 venues. 40+ artists. 4,000+ people. Port Kembla Festival is everything a community event should be — live independent music, markets, art, good people, and good vibes all round. The fact that it’s free and community-funded makes it even more special.
Thanks for having us, Port Kembla Festival — it was an honour to be part of something so unique. 🙌

The plate you eat from shapes the meal itself. Nabila Nareswari works in nerikomi ceramics, layering coloured clay into intricate, patterned forms that are as much about feeling as function. For Nabila, the object isn’t just a container. It’s part of the story being told at every meal.

At our #UFF26 Chef’s Table you get up close with the crew as they craft their signature dishes right before your eyes. Fresh from the pan and grill, here are our top picks you don’t want to miss.

Ben Devlin, master of Gyotaku, presses fresh fish to paper, a ghost-print of the morning’s catch. Then the fire. Simon Polkinghorne of Masonry Canggu takes the pit with charred prawns, whole fish, and wagyu. The catch, the flame, the table.

Over at another session, Andres Becerra of Santanera and Frank Camorra of MoVida bring their Gentleman’s Paella, saffron-rich bomba rice slow-cooked over fire and finished with tender calamari. Patience, depth, and instinct, plated live.

Or pull up a seat for Chef Bernard Chew as he takes the pass to prepare his famous Soft Shell Singaporean Chili Crab live. Fiery, tangy, rich, and unapologetically bold, a family recipe plated in real time.

Seats are limited. Secure yours before they are gone. Book your spot through our website at tinyurl.com/UFF26ChefsTable today.

🎧 Now, the work continues as a self-guided performance at the Centro Cultural da Caloura, open to anyone wishing to experience this mountain body that breathes beneath the sea.

Durante o fim de semana de Abertura, ao nascer e pôr do sol, convidou os participantes a flutuar e a explorar o mar com pequenas esculturas de madeira à deriva, recolhidas em diferentes ilhas do arquipélago.

🎧 Agora, a experiência continua como uma performance auto-guiada no Centro Cultural da Caloura, aberta a quem quiser descobrir este corpo montanhoso que respira sob o mar.

Designed by architect Nuno Pimenta, 𝐶𝐴𝑆𝐴 𝐷𝐴 𝐵𝐼𝐸𝑁𝐴𝐿 is open to visitors, with information about the program, an area for lounging and resting, books and almanacs for consultation, and a screening room with the video essay Ecotone. – (Walk&Talk souvenirs are also available!)

Almanacs serve as an entry point to imagine
geography through situated relations and knowledges. Blending weather forecasts, planetary routes, agricultural advice, and popular wisdom, they operate as alternative maps — weaving time, attention, and experience into a collective intelligence that spans generations. 

𝑬𝒄𝒐𝒕𝒐𝒏𝒆, a video essay by Enar de Dios Rodríguez, extends this reflection. Like an almanac, it becomes a repository of migrations, observations, and narratives.

📍Praça do Município, 4, Ponta Delgada
🕐 Open until 𝟐𝟗.𝟏𝟏 | Tuesday to Saturday, 11H–18H

🧵The space is generously provided by @levelconstellationlisboa.

|

Pensada pelo arquiteto Nuno Pimenta, a 𝐶𝐴𝑆𝐴 𝐷𝐴 𝐵𝐼𝐸𝑁𝐴𝐿 está aberta a visitantes, com informações sobre o programa,  uma área para descansar e conviver, livros e almanaques para consulta, merchandising, e a exibição do vídeo-ensaio Ecotone. – (Souvenirs Walk&Talk também disponíveis!) 

Os almanaques servem como ponto de entrada para imaginar a geografia através de relações e saberes situados. Misturando previsões meteorológicas, rotas planetárias, conselhos agrícolas e sabedoria popular, funcionam como mapas alternativos — tecendo tempo, atenção e experiência numa inteligência coletiva que atravessa gerações. 

𝑬𝒄𝒐𝒕𝒐𝒏𝒆, o vídeo-ensaio de Enar de Dios Rodríguez, prolonga esta reflexão. Tal como um almanaque, torna-se repositório de migrações, observações e narrativas.

The sea is a territory of multiple layers: an affective archive, a space of displacement, a site of extraction, a surface of projection, a repository of violence. The works gathered in this station activate the ocean as a living, sensitive, and political matter — refusing its reduction to a natural resource or a touristic postcard.

In doing so, they open questions that traverse postcolonial thought, ecological critique, and feminist and queer epistemologies: how can we resist the extractivist logic that turns waters and lives into commodities? How can we reinscribe affective geographies emerging from routes of migration, trade, and diaspora? Which historical imaginaries remain to be reconstituted — or reinvented — from the ocean?

📍Largo Mártires da Pátria, 17, Ponta Delgada
👀 Open until 𝟐𝟗.𝟏𝟏 | Monday to Friday, 09H–17H. Saturday, 14h–17H.

|

O mar é um território de muitas camadas: arquivo de afetos, espaço de deslocação, lugar de extração, superfície de projeção, mas também repositório de violências. As obras reunidas nesta estação ativam o oceano como matéria viva, sensível e política — recusando a sua redução a recurso natural ou a postal turístico. 

Ao fazê-lo, abrem questões que atravessam o pensamento pós-colonial, a crítica ecológica e as epistemologias feministas e queer: como resistir à lógica extrativista que transforma águas e vidas em mercadoria? Como reinscrever geografias afetivas que emergem de rotas de migração, de comércio e de diáspora? Que imaginários históricos permanecem por reconstituir — ou reinventar — a partir do oceano?

—
📸 @marianalidl

An audiovisual journey through artistic practices that engage with territories in transformation — geographic, affective, spiritual, ecological, and political. The selection draws from the theme of the biennial, 𝐺𝐸𝑆𝑇𝑈𝑅𝐸𝑆 𝑂𝐹 𝐴𝐵𝑈𝑁𝐷𝐴𝑁𝐶𝐸.

Three works unfold as visual essays on what it means to coexist in times of transformation:

The Being of Relation, 2022 (ro heinrich)
The thought of Indigenous Brazilian leader Ailton Krenak and the voices of several interlocutors, including Erin Manning, open a meditative space on being as relation — a film that lingers in the trembling edges of difference, touch, and transformation. 

BeastQuest, 2025 (Kolbeinn Hugi) @animal.internet
Combines humour and science fiction to imagine a digital creature entering the ecological simulation GAIANET to configure a server for the Animal Internet — a techno-shamanic delirium where nature and cyberspace become interdependent.

Soy Much, 2021 (Soya the Cow) @soyathecow
A queer, vegan pop manifesto celebrating freedom and the abundance of dissident bodies — human and non-human alike — through music, irony, and the assertion of difference.

In this station, abundance is conceived as reverberation — what echoes, what persists, what becomes visible when we see and listen with time, attention, and openness. Against an idea of visibility as totality, the works presented here operate through subtlety, deviation, and displacement.

The ADORE Chef’s Table is an industry-focused showcase highlighting the elevation of Indonesian cacao and vanilla. The event begins with an interactive “Aroma Bar”, where Executive Chefs and hospitality leaders can explore raw fermented Bali single-origin cacao beans and premium vanilla pods. This opening creates a sophisticated space for the F&B community to network while discovering the foundational science of flavour at its source.

The programme features a technical demonstration by Dessert Masters winner Gareth Whitton, followed by a “Fireside Conversation” with ADORE founder Riza Kamal. Moderated by the Bali Restaurant and Café Association, the discussion explores the connection between craftsmanship and ingredient consistency — sharing insights into how Gareth maintains the signature quality of Tarts Anon and how ADORE’s scientific approach supports the demands of a modern professional kitchen.

The experience concludes with a curated tasting of Gareth’s signature tarts, showcasing the application of Bali single-origin dark chocolate and premium vanilla. This final phase invites guests to experience the ingredients in a refined culinary setting, celebrating the collaboration between global culinary expertise and Indonesian ingredient mastery in an intimate and conversational atmosphere.

This is a private event and by invitation only.

Through a live cooking demonstration, discover the cultural meaning and traditions behind papeda, the comforting sweetness of sagu pisang from Jailolo, and a nourishing herbal drink rooted in local wisdom. The experience continues around a long communal table, where participants will enjoy a specially prepared early dinner featuring kuah kuning and fresh ikan gohu, a vibrant celebration of North Maluku’s coastal flavours. More than a cooking class, this is an invitation to taste a part of Indonesia rarely seen, and to experience how food can connect us to place, history, and one another.

This event is curated and hosted by Helianti Hilman and supported by Bank Indonesia KpW Maluku Utara.

The price includes an early dinner tasting experience and welcome drink.

Four Hands. One table. A cuisine shaped by the forest.

At the heart of this luncheon are the women defenders of Indonesia’s forests, farmers, foragers, seed keepers and guardians of ancestral knowledge. Representing communities from South Sumatera, Kalimantan and West Nusa Tenggara, Jamuan Puan Rimba carries generations of wisdom on wild foods, fire, healing herbs and the fragile ecosystems that sustain them. Their hands, stories and resilience form the soul of this table.

Joining them are Helianti Hilman of Javara, Indonesia’s leading voice in biodiversity and food sovereignty; Agus Hermawan, the Amsterdam-based Indonesian chef reframing his homeland for the world; and Bambu Indah’s own Chef Aaron Lumakeki, whose kitchen shares the same philosophy: that food is memory, land is sacred, and cooking is an act of preservation.

Set around a communal table overlooking a lush organic garden, the afternoon unfolds through bold flavours, ancient rhythms and local tonics. River fish meets flame. Jungle greens and wild herbs reveal forgotten landscapes. Chili lingers long after the last bite.

This is more than a meal. It is a tribute to the women who protect the forest, and the knowledge that still grows within it. Come hungry. Leave transformed. Seats are limited.

Like a seismograph, this station records tremors, movements, and intensities that escape the immediate gaze, opening space for tactile, sensory, and spiritual forms of knowledge. In Caloura, the works gathered expand the sensitive field of the territory: they listen to seismic tremors, aquatic fluctuations, mineral layers, and botanical fictions. The earth is no longer conceived as a resource or a stable surface, but revealed instead as a body in transformation — unstable and relational. 

Drawing from the volcanic geology of the Azores, this proposal is a listening practice that unfolds into attentiveness and political imagination. Here, abundance, is porosity: a territory where matter, spirit, and landscape intertwine, inviting us to inhabit the world in slower, more interdependent, and more imaginative compositions.

📍Canada do Castelo, Água de Pau, Lagoa
👀 Open until 𝟐𝟗.𝟏𝟏 | Monday to Saturday, 10H30–12H30 / 13H30–17H30.

Como um sismógrafo, esta estação regista abalos e movimentos que escapam ao olhar imediato, abrindo espaço para formas de conhecimento táteis e sensoriais. Na Caloura, os trabalhos expandem o campo sensível do território: em sintonia com vibrações sísmicas, flutuações aquáticas, estratos minerais e ficções botânicas. A terra surge não como recurso ou solo estável, mas como um corpo em transformação — instável e relacional. 

A partir da geologia vulcânica dos Açores, a proposta aqui é uma prática de escuta que se desdobra em atenção e imaginação política. A abundância torna-se porosidade — um território onde matéria, espírito e paisagem se entrelaçam, convidando-nos a habitar o mundo de formas mais lentas e interdependentes.

🎥: @lmjw_

Hooooooly! Our GA passes are SOLD OUT.

Feeling deeply grateful 🙏🏼 

We still have a handful of day passes available 🙌🏼

…now let’s party 🥳

Sauna Fest 26 💧💨🌱🔥

What a surreal experience. 
To see so many good people together in one place, elevating each other’s energy, is hard to put into words. I feel like we broke into new territory, redefining what it means to have fun and feel safe.

Some say we got lucky, some say we had it all planned, neither are totally true. But what we do know is that what happened was something special, and we plan on continuing this festival well into the future, creating a place for culture to grow and norms to be redefined.

Festivals play a vital role in the cultural development of a country, and we plan on Sauna Fest being there, using saunas as our vehicle to give musicians a platform to play to an engaged crowd, and presenters a space to share their knowledge.

Stitching all of this together is our mission, and we promise not to alter our core values.

We will most likely sell out fairly quickly in the coming years and, as festival organisers, this gives us the luxury of focusing on the details of the festival experience rather than stressing about selling enough tickets to make sure everyone involved gets paid.

Selling out a festival is good for everyone involved, and we plan on refining every part of the experience, making each year better than the last.

Thank you to everyone who contributed and for being a part of our community, it means the world.

🌱💨💧🔥

The Sauna Fest schedule is officially LIVE.

This year is something special.

For the first time ever, we’re hosting the Aufguss Championship. Across the weekend, there will be guided sauna performances every hour, with each contestant bringing their own style, story, and energy into the sauna.

We’re also bringing some saunas right to the lakefront, giving you a true sauna to lake experience. You’ll be able to step straight from the heat into the water. It’s simple, powerful, and unlike anything we’ve done before.

One of the highlights of the weekend will be Dr. Richard Drexel, a highly respected holistic doctor known for his incredible work with patients. He’ll be speaking on Saturday, with a follow up session on Sunday. These are not to be missed.

Across the weekend, you’ll find hourly Aufguss Championship sessions, daily run club around the Blue Lake with Run Aotearoa, and plenty of sauna, cold water, music, and connection.

A big highlight this year is Casual Healing taking to the main stage for our sunset session. From there, the energy carries into the night with two stages running simultaneously, with DJs playing through until around 1am. The vibe will be alive as the energy carries through the night.

Everything is included in your GA ticket. There are no bookings required. Just arrive, explore the schedule, and follow what calls you.

This week I finally had a little play with fresh indigo, and  it was a delight 🌿
Last year at Sauna Fest I ran a workshop making sauna hats from NZ wool, dyed with food waste - avocado pips and onion skins which created very earthy tones. This year I’m bringing along a new colour palette, gathered from plants we can grow right in our own backyards.

Indigo is such a fabulous dye plant, not needing pre mordanting, and giving a beautiful range of blues. 

What a treat it was to work slowly, outdoors, hands in the process, learning as I go and letting the results unfold in their own time.

Next time I think I will wear gloves 😅

Not just for contests. Not just for skating.

But to create opportunities. Community. Inspiration. A place where young skaters can challenge themselves, be seen, gain confidence, and chase something bigger.

Behind achievements like this are years of work, commitment, sacrifice, progression, support from family, and an athlete who kept showing up.

Who might be skating at SKATESIDE FEST 2026 right now?

Who’s building toward their own story?

The next champion. The next national qualifier. The next athlete inspiring a generation.

Huge congratulations Julian. Thank you for inspiring our community and showing what’s possible. 👏🇺🇸

caption:
NZ Aufguss Championship 🔥💧

Sauna Fest 26 will host the first ever NZ Aufguss Championship!

The Aufguss has become a signature part of The Sauna Project experience. It’s where water is poured onto the rocks while silence is held, and then the air, mixed with essential oils, is moved around the sauna with a towel.

Aufguss championships are a big thing in European countries, and representing your country at these championships is a big deal.

We’re doing our own version of it. We have over 15 contestants who will each create two fifteen minute experiences in the sauna. They will take the people inside on a journey through heat waves, music, essential oils and much more. Even storytelling could be involved.

We will create a schedule so you know when each session is happening and where.

This is the first of its kind in NZ and is our attempt to bring authentic sauna culture here while giving it a Kiwi twist.

This is an experience you don’t want to miss.

Tickets are in our bio.

Confidence doesn’t happen by accident 🛹💥

One of the biggest reasons kids gain so much confidence at THE SKATESIDE is because we focus on the SMALL STEPS first.

Before students learn tricks, ramps, or advanced skills, we teach:
✔ How to stand correctly
✔ How to balance safely
✔ How to fall safely
✔ How to stop and control the board
✔ How to use their pads properly
✔ How to build comfort step-by-step

We repeat these foundations over and over until students truly feel ready.

A lot of programs rush kids into things before they are comfortable. That’s where fear, frustration, and injuries can happen.

At THE SKATESIDE, if a student is not ready, we simply slow down and continue practicing the basics. No pressure. No embarrassment. Just progress at the right pace.

Safety is a HUGE part of our program:
🛹 Helmets are mandatory
🛹 Pads are mandatory
🛹 Safety always comes first

When kids feel protected and supported, they become more willing to try again — and that’s where confidence starts to grow.

Another major difference is our coaching staff.

We are not just grabbing random skaters at a skatepark and saying “hey, teach these kids.”

Every coach is trained through THE SKATESIDE system and learns how to teach kids the SKATESIDE way:
💙 Patience
💙 Safety
💙 Encouragement
💙 Structure
💙 Positive communication
💙 Age-appropriate progression

Being good at skateboarding does NOT automatically make someone good at teaching children.

That’s why our staff are trained to safely teach beginners, build confidence, manage groups, and create a positive environment where students feel supported and successful.

Over time, those small wins become:
🔥 Bigger confidence
🔥 More independence
🔥 Resilience
🔥 Trust in themselves

Since 2015, THE SKATESIDE has helped thousands of kids grow through skateboarding and roller skating — one small step at a time 💙

What it looks like: just a ramp.
What it feels like: overcoming fear for the first time.

From the outside, it may not seem like much. A small ramp. A short roll-in. Just another turn at the skatepark.

But for a child standing at the top, it can feel huge.
Heart racing. Hands tight on the board. Questions running through their mind: What if I fall? What if I can’t do it?

And then something powerful happens.
They try anyway.

That moment isn’t just about skateboarding. It’s about learning how to face challenges, trust themselves, and discover that they are capable of more than they thought.

At THE SKATESIDE, we see it every day. Confidence doesn’t appear overnight. It’s built one small victory at a time — one attempt, one smile, one brave drop-in.

Because today it’s a ramp.
Tomorrow it’s school, friendships, goals, and life.

Confidence starts in moments like these. 🛹

Fear shows up for every kid at the skatepark.

The drop-in looks big.
The ramp feels fast.
The board feels wobbly.

And in that moment, a lot of kids think the same thing:

“I can’t do this.”

This week at camp we interviewed one of our campers after he landed something he had been afraid to try. When we asked him how he finally did it, his answer captured exactly what we intentionally build into THE SKATESIDE program.

We coached him to think positively and tell himself out loud:

“I can do this.”

Not once.
Over and over again.

“I can do this.
I can do this.
I can do this.”

At first he didn’t fully believe it.

But he kept saying it anyway.
He kept stepping up.
He kept trying.

And eventually… he did it.

That moment right there is exactly why THE SKATESIDE exists.

Yes, kids learn how to skateboard.
Yes, they learn tricks, balance, and coordination.

But we intentionally teach something deeper.

We teach kids how to speak to themselves when things feel hard.

Because that inner voice becomes the one they carry with them for the rest of their lives.

When a child learns at 8, 9, or 10 years old that they can face fear, encourage themselves, try again, and eventually succeed… that lesson doesn’t stay at the skatepark.

It follows them into school.
Into friendships.
Into sports.
Into adulthood.

Years from now, when that same kid faces something difficult — a big test, a challenge, a new opportunity — they will remember the feeling of standing on that board, nervous but determined, repeating to themselves:

“I can do this.”

And then proving it.

That’s why what we do matters.

It’s not just learning tricks.
It’s about building confident kids who believe in themselves.

This session opens with a provocation: “Farmers guard the land and sea. But who guards the knowledge of what grows there and why it matters?” The session is structured as a conversation between two practitioners with complementary perspectives: one working at the level of frameworks and policy, the other embedded in community and cultural life.

O Come Closer by Toyota leva o Porto/Post/Doc ao Vodafone Paredes de Coura com sete sessões gratuitas no Centro Cultural de Paredes de Coura. Um filme por dia, às 14:00. 

Hoje, abrimos com "Deuses de Pedra", de Iván Castiñeiras Gallego. Filmado ao longo de quinze anos entre a Galiza e Portugal, o documentário acompanha uma comunidade rural onde as histórias de infância se confundem com lendas ancestrais e onde o tempo transforma aqueles que a habitam. No centro está Mariana que, aos 17 anos, terá de decidir entre permanecer na aldeia com a mãe ou partir para o estrangeiro em busca de um futuro.

Com estreia mundial no Festival de Roterdão, "Deuses de Pedra" venceu o Prémio do Júri para Melhor Filme Nacional e o Prémio CineZeta do Júri Jovem no Documenta Madrid, e foi distinguido como Melhor Filme Galego no Play-Doc.

⚫️ 9 ago, 14:00, Centro Cultural de Paredes de Coura

✨ SKATESIDE FEST MAGIC IN THE MAKING ✨
If you’ve never seen a kid design their own skateboard from scratch… you’ve never seen pure creativity in action.

At SKATESIDE FEST, our Build-Your-Own Skateboard Station is where imagination explodes. Kids sketch, paint, color, and dream on their decks — turning a simple piece of wood into something that’s 100% theirs. No limits, no rules, just expression.

You can literally watch their confidence grow in real time:
🖍️ Choosing colors that feel bold
🎨 Drawing characters and symbols that tell their story
🛹 Designing a board they can’t wait to ride on day one

It’s more than a craft.
It’s a moment where their ideas matter.
Where their voices show up as art.
Where they realize, “I made this… and I can ride it.”

These boards go home as keepsakes, memories, and powerful reminders of what kids can create when they feel supported, celebrated, and seen.

SKATESIDE FEST is all about building confidence, community, and the next generation of skaters — one deck at a time. 💙🛹✨
More kids skating. More kids creating. More kids believing in themselves.
